IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r6.claim: The supplicant is like someone stretching hands toward water to scoop it and bring it to his mouth; that action is left implicit.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r6.anchor: أراد: كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليقبض عليه فيبلغه فاه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r7.speaker: ضابئ
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r7.claim: Ḍābiʾ’s poem compares longing without fulfillment to clutching water that the fingers cannot hold; Arabs use the same expression for futile pursuit.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r7.anchor:
قال ضابىء :
فإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p273/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p273/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p273/r1.claim: An unnamed man afflicted with a camel-like swelling returned to al-Sululiyya's home repeating his fate, died on horseback, and the passage about secret and public speech through disbelievers' prayer was revealed about him.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p273/r1.anchor: كغدة البعير، فعاد إلى بيت السلولية وهو يقول: غدة كغدة البعير وموت في بيت السلولية، ثم مات على ظهر فرسه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi rejects the codices' Madinan classification: in his view, the sūra is wholly Makkan, with no Madinan verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some codices regard it to be Madī nan, which I fail to understand. Not one of its verse is Mad īnan in my opinion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Calling on anyone besides God resembles chasing a mirage; self-appointed deities and intercessors cannot benefit anyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Invoking someone other than God is like regarding a mirage to be water and then running after it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r16.claim: The palm is the familiar hand; its small plural is akuff and its larger plural kufūf, while its root is a verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r16.anchor: الكف: عضو معروف، وجمعه في القلة أكف كصك وأصك، وفي الكثرة كفوف كصكوك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p342/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p342/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p342/r3.claim: Another Meccan report excepts the passage from the sign of lightning through the statement that the true call belongs to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p342/r3.anchor: وعن غيره إلا قوله: هو الذي يريكم البرق إلى قوله: له دعوة الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p365#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p365#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p365#2/r11.claim: The pronoun in له refers to God; Ibn ʿAbbās defines دعوة الحق as the declaration lā ilāha illā Allāh and related elements of the religious law.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p365#2/r11.anchor: والضمير في له عائد على الله تعالى، ودعوة الحق قال ابن عباس: دعوة الحق لا إله إلا الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r1.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib says دعوة الحق means God's oneness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r1.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب، دعوة الحق التوحيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God is al-Ḥaqq, so invoking Him is an invocation of the truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: إن الله هو الحق، فدعاؤه دعوة الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r3.claim: Another interpretation makes دعوة الحق a plea to God in moments of fear, when no one else is called; al-Māwardī says this best suits the context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r3.anchor: وقيل: دعوة الحق دعاؤه عند الخوف، فإنه لا يدعى فيه إلا هو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r4.claim: Another interpretation understands it as a true request that is hoped to be answered, unlike supplication to anyone besides God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r4.anchor: وقيل: دعوة الطلب الحق أي: مرجو الإجابة، ودعاء غير الله لا يجاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's first analysis attaches the invocation to truth as opposed to falsehood: God alone is rightly invoked and grants a useful request when it benefits the supplicant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r5.anchor: أن تضاف الدعوة إلى الحق الذي هو نقيض الباطل، كما تضاف الكلمة إليه في قوله: «كلمة الحق»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's second analysis takes al-Ḥaqq to mean God, the true one who hears and answers; al-Ḥasan says every prayer to God is an invocation of truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r6.anchor: أن تضاف إلى الحق الذي هو الله عز وجل على معنى دعوة المدعو الحق الذي يسمع فيجيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's second analysis because it amounts to the awkward wording 'God has God's invocation.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r7.anchor: وهذا الوجه الثاني الذي ذكره الزمخشري لا يظهر، لأن مآله إلى تقدير: لله دعوة الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r8.claim: He prefers construing the phrase as a qualified noun plus attribute: God owns the true invocation, unlike the false invocations of the idols under discussion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r8.anchor: والذي يظهر أن هذه الإضافة من باب إضافة الموصوف إلى الصفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that idols cannot answer requests, like water that does not respond when someone stretches hands toward it asking it to reach the mouth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p366/r9.anchor: والآلهة الذين يدعونهم الكفار من دون الله لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء من طلباتهم إلا استجابة كاستجابة باسط كفيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r1.claim: Idols are inanimate, unaware of their worshippers' prayers, unable to answer, and unable to benefit them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r1.anchor: وكذلك ما يدعونه جماد لا يحس بدعائهم، ولا يستطيع إجابتهم، ولا يقدر على نفعهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r2.claim: Another comparison depicts futile prayer as spreading open hands to scoop water, which slips away and never provides a drink.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r2.anchor: فبسطهما ناشرا أصابعه فلم تبق كفاه منه شيئا، ولم يبلغ طلبته من شربه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r3.claim: On one parsing, the subject of يدعون is the idolaters and the object pronoun is omitted; the tāʾ reading تدعون, transmitted by al-Yazīdī from Abū ʿAmr, supports it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r3.anchor: فالضمير في يدعون عائد على الكفار، والعائد على الذين محذوف أي: يدعونهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r4.claim: An alternative makes الذين refer to the idolaters who invoke idols, with the object of يدعون omitted; the two later plural verbs then refer either to the idols or to the relative antecedent, depending on the parsing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r4.anchor: وقيل: الذين أي: الكفار الذين يدعون، ومفعول يدعون محذوف أي: يدعون الأصنام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares the idolater to someone looking at his reflection in water and trying to seize it: imagined help remains only an illusion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كالناظر إلى خياله في الماء يريد تناوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r6.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk likens the worshipper to someone reaching for water without scooping it up.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كمن بسط يديه إلى الماء ليصل إليه بلا اغتراف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda calls it grasping water and holding nothing; Arabs use this for pursuing the unattainable, and a line cited by Sībawayh illustrates the idiom.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: أي كالقابض على الماء ليس على شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r8.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r8.claim: Sībawayh cites a poem comparing a lost relationship to grasping water in one's hand, illustrating the proverb for futile effort.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r8.anchor: فأصبحت فيما كان بيني وبينها ... من الود مثل القابض الماء في اليد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r9.claim: Another explanation pictures desperate idolaters at a well calling to water to quench their thirst; neither can reach the other, just as idols cannot hear or help.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r9.anchor: برجل عطشان لا يقدر على الماء، جلس على شفير بئر يدعو الماء ليبل غلته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r10.claim: The kāf is accusative as a comparison; istijābat is a verbal noun annexed to its object, while its subject is understood as water answering the person who reaches out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r10.anchor: والكاف في موضع نصب أي: مثل استجابة، واستجابة مضافة في التقدير إلى باسط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says those whom idolaters call on for needs never answer, just as water never reaches the mouth of someone who gestures toward it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ومعنى الكلام الذي يدعونهم الكفار إلى حوائجهم ومنافعهم لا يجيبون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r12.claim: In ليبلغ, the subject can be water and the object the mouth, or the subject can be the mouth and the object water; neither reaches the other in this situation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r12.anchor: وفاعل ليبلغ ضمير الماء، وليبلغ متعلق بباسط، وما هو أي: وما الماء ببالغه، أي: ببالغ الفم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r14.claim: The disbelievers' invocation is in bewilderment or loss because it yields nothing and the invoked beings have themselves gone astray.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r14.anchor: أي: في حيرة، أو في اضمحلال، لأنه لا يجدي شيئا ولا يفيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the phrase as wasted effort: God does not answer their invocation, and the idols cannot answer either.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r15.anchor: إلا في ضياع لا منفعة فيه، لأنهم إن دعوا الله لم يجبهم، وإن دعوا الآلهة لم نستطع إجابتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the disbelievers' voices are veiled from God, so He does not hear their supplication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p367/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أصوات الكافرين محجوبة عن الله فلا يسمع دعاءهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.claim: Al-Raʿd’s aim is to portray revelation as true in itself: sometimes its sound and fame move people toward guidance, while sometimes it instead leaves them blind and astray, like thunder whose lightning and rain may benefit, fail, or harm according to where they fall.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.anchor: مقصودها وصف الكتاب بأنه الحق في نفسه ، وتارة يتأثر عنه مع أن له صوتا وصيتا وإرعابا وإرهابا

DURR-FULL:v4p617/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p617/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p617/r1.claim: The report concludes that lightning killed Arbad and plague killed Amir; Ibn Zayd links their story to the verses on hidden and spoken words, protecting angels, and the futility of disbelievers' prayers.
DURR-FULL:v4p617/r1.anchor: فخرج أربد حتى إذا كان بالرقم بعث الله سحابة من الصيف فيها صاعقة فأحرقته وخرج عامر حتى إذا كان بوادي الحريد أرسل الله عليه الطاعون

NAHHAS:v2p353/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p353/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p353/r13.claim: Daʿwā al-kāfirīn means their calling upon idols, which is futile, far from right and unable to bring a response.
NAHHAS:v2p353/r13.anchor: أي وما دعاء الكافرين الأوثان ( إلا في ضلال ) عن الصواب وعن الانتفاع بالإجابة

THALABI:v5p280/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p280/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p280/r8.claim: Daʿwat al-ḥaqq means the true invocation; the phrase joins two different nouns.
THALABI:v5p280/r8.anchor: له لله عز وجل دعوة الحق الصدق وأضيفت الدعوة إلى الحق لاختلاف الاسمين

THALABI:v5p280/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p280/r9.speaker: علي
THALABI:v5p280/r9.claim: Ali identifies the true invocation as monotheism.
THALABI:v5p280/r9.anchor: قال علي (رضي الله عنه) : دعوة الحق التوحيد.

THALABI:v5p280/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p280/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p280/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the true invocation as the testimony that there is no deity but God.
THALABI:v5p280/r10.anchor: ابن عباس (رضي الله عنه) : شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله.

STUDYQURAN:13:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r1.speaker: AF, Kl, My
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r1.claim: AF, Kl, and My identify the supplication of truth with the shahādah, “There is no god but God.”
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r1.anchor: lā ilāha illa’Llāh; AF, Kl, My

STUDYQURAN:13:14/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r2.claim: More broadly, the phrase can mean any supplication that God accepts and answers, as in 40:60.
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r2.anchor: More generally, it can refer to any form of supplication that God accepts and to which He responds, as in 40:60: Call upon Me, and I shall respond to you

STUDYQURAN:13:14/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r3.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r3.claim: Kl explains that true supplication is directed to God, while supplication to anything else is futile.
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r3.anchor: The supplication of truth therefore is supplication to God, whereas the supplication to what is other than Him is futile (Kl)

STUDYQURAN:13:14/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r4.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r4.claim: Those whom disbelievers supplicate apart from God are idols and false gods.
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r4.anchor: as is the case with those whom they—that is, the disbelievers—supplicate apart from Him, namely, idols and false gods (Z).

STUDYQURAN:13:14/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r5.claim: False gods cannot hear or answer because they have no power to bring harm or benefit; other verses stress their powerlessness.
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r5.anchor: The false gods that people call upon other than God answer them not in the least, because they do not have the ability to bring about harm or benefit

STUDYQURAN:13:14/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r6.claim: On the Last Day, the false gods will not be able to answer those who called to them for help.
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r6.anchor: This is why, on the Last Day, they will not be able to answer those who called upon them for help

STUDYQURAN:13:14/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r7.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r7.claim: The analogy likens futile invocation to hands stretched toward water that cannot perceive the gesture, just as false gods cannot hear or respond.
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r7.anchor: just as the water cannot perceive that his hands are outstretched for it, so too are those whom one calls upon apart from God unable to hear his supplications and respond to them (Z).

STUDYQURAN:13:14/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r8.claim: The closing statement repeats a portion of 40:50.
STUDYQURAN:13:14/r8.anchor: And the supplication of the disbelievers is naught but astray is identical to a portion of 40:50.

TAB-FULL:v13p485/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r1.claim: The true call belongs to Allah; al-Tabari identifies it as affirming God's oneness and testifying that there is no deity but Allah.
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r1.anchor: وإنما عنى بالدعوة الحق: توحيد الله، وشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

TAB-FULL:v13p485/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r2.claim: The phrase means the call itself is the truth, expressed through an iḍāfa like دار الآخرة in 12:109.
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r2.anchor: قوله: {ولدار الآخرة} [يوسف: 109] وقد بينا ذلك فيما مضى

TAB-FULL:v13p485/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the true call as لا إله إلا الله, or the testimony that there is no deity but Allah.
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: " {دعوة الحق} [الرعد: 14] قال: لا إله إلا الله "

TAB-FULL:v13p485/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r4.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r4.claim: Ali interprets the true call as monotheism.
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r4.anchor: عن أبي أيوب، عن علي، رضي الله عنه: " {له دعوة الحق} [الرعد: 14] قال: التوحيد "

TAB-FULL:v13p485/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r5.claim: Qatada identifies the true call as لا إله إلا الله.
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {له دعوة الحق} [الرعد: 14] قال: لا إله إلا الله "

TAB-FULL:v13p485/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v13p485/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says only Allah merits the true call and that none should be called a deity besides Him.

TAB-FULL:v13p487/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p487/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p487/r1.claim: Those called upon besides Allah are idols that polytheists invoke as lords and gods; min dunihi means apart from Allah, and these deficient objects cannot be gods, since only Allah is God. The cited usage of dun means falling short of someone.
TAB-FULL:v13p487/r1.anchor: الشاعر: [البحر الوافر] أتوعدني وراء بني رياح … كذبت، لتقصرن يداك دوني

TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r1.claim: The invoked idols do not answer requests for benefit or protection from harm; calling on them is as useless as extending empty hands to water without drawing it into a vessel.
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r1.anchor: في إناء، ولكن ليرتفع إليه بدعائه إياه وإشارته إليه وقبضه عليه

TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r2.claim: The image evokes an impossible effort; Arabs liken pursuing what cannot be attained to grasping water, as the cited poems illustrate.
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r2.anchor: والعرب تضرب لمن سعى فيما لا يدركه مثلا بالقابض على الماء

TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r3.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r3.claim: Ali compares the image to a thirsty man reaching into a well and hoping the water will rise to him, which it cannot do.
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r3.anchor: عن علي، رضي الله عنه، في قوله: {إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه}

TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says the person calls to the water with his tongue and gestures with his hand, but it never comes; so too those invoked besides Allah do not answer.
TAB-FULL:v13p487#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {كباسط كفيه إلى الماء} [الرعد: 14] «يدعو الماء بلسانه، ويشير إليه بيده

TAB-FULL:v13p489/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p489/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p489/r1.claim: Qatada depicts the water as unreachable until the thirsty person tears his neck apart and dies of thirst.
TAB-FULL:v13p489/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه

TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r1.claim: Calling on an idol or stone never brings good or wards off harm, and the worshipper remains without benefit until death, like one who dies thirsty with outstretched arms.
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r1.anchor: يبلغ فاه ولا يصل إليه ذلك حتى يموت عطشا.

TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r2.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas compares the polytheist to a thirsty man who sees his reflection in distant water and cannot grasp it.
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه} [الرعد: 14]

TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas pictures a dying thirsty person's hands in water but unable to reach his mouth; likewise idols never answer or benefit their worshippers.
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء} [الرعد: 14]

TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the idols do no more good than hands extended toward something that can never be reached.
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء

TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r5.claim: Qatada says water cannot reach the mouth while the hands remain outstretched, just as an adopted deity cannot benefit its worshipper or protect him from harm until death.
TAB-FULL:v13p489#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: {إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه} [الرعد: 14] " وليس الماء ببالغ فاه

TABATABAI:13:12-14/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r11.claim: Duʿāʾ directs the one summoned to attend to the caller, usually by speech or gesture; response is the summoned one's turning toward the caller.
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r11.anchor: الدعاء والدعوة توجيه نظر المدعو إلى الداعي ويتأتى غالبا بلفظ أو إشارة

TABATABAI:13:12-14/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r12.claim: Requesting a need and fulfilling it complete the ideas of invocation and response, but are not part of their basic meanings.
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r12.anchor: غاية متممة لمعنى الدعاء والاستجابة غير داخلة في مفهوميهما

TABATABAI:13:12-14/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r13.claim: A real invocation requires an addressee capable of perceiving the caller and of answering; addressing the unaware or powerless is only invocation in outward form.
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r13.anchor: دعاء حقيقة إذا كان المدعو ذا نظر يمكن أن يوجه إلى الداعي وذا جدة وقدرة

TABATABAI:13:12-14/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r14.claim: The contrast with unanswered calls and the description of unbelievers’ invocation as lost show that God's is the true call, which He hears and unfailingly answers; He is near, responsive, rich, and merciful.
TABATABAI:13:12-14/r14.anchor: علمنا بذلك أن المراد بقوله { دعوة الحق } الدعوة الحقة غير الباطلة وهي الدعوة التي يسمعها المدعو ثم يستجيبها البتة

TABATABAI:13:14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r1.claim: The phrase can be read as an attributive annexation, or as a true annexation that treats truth and falsehood as dividing invocations between effective and futile calls.
TABATABAI:13:14/r1.anchor: فلفظة دعوة الحق من إضافة الموصوف إلى الصفة أو من الإضافة الحقيقية بعناية أن الحق والباطل كأنهما يقتسمان الدعاء

TABATABAI:13:14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r2.claim: God's unqualified promises to answer the caller support the reading that He alone possesses the true invocation and response.
TABATABAI:13:14/r2.anchor: أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان البقرة 186 وقال ادعوني أستجب لكم غافر 60

TABATABAI:13:14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r3.claim: Placing the prepositional phrase first restricts the true invocation to God, a restriction reinforced by the following denial of response from other objects of worship.
TABATABAI:13:14/r3.anchor: وتقديم الظرف يفيد الحصر ويؤيده ما بعده من نفيه عن غيره

TABATABAI:13:14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r4.claim: After describing God's knowledge and power, the verse adds His true invocation and response, asserting this exclusively for Him and denying it of all others.
TABATABAI:13:14/r4.anchor: ذكر ذلك في الآية بطريقي الإثبات والنفي أعني إثبات حق الدعاء لنفسه ونفيه عن غيره

TABATABAI:13:14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r5.claim: The invoked beings are either lifeless idols called on by ordinary people or, as their more informed devotees recognize, angels, jinn, astral spirits, and humans; none controls benefit, harm, life, death, or resurrection.
TABATABAI:13:14/r5.anchor: فإن هؤلاء المدعوين إما أصنام يدعوهم عامتهم وهي أجسام ميتة لا شعور فيها ولا إرادة

TABATABAI:13:14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r6.claim: All dominion and power belong to God, so there is no hope of response from any other being.
TABATABAI:13:14/r6.anchor: ولله الملك كله وله القوة كلها فلا مطمع عند غيره تعالى

TABATABAI:13:14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r7.claim: A thirsty person near water can approach, scoop it, and drink; someone far away who only stretches out his hands can never reach it, so his effort has only the appearance of seeking.
TABATABAI:13:14/r7.anchor: فإن الإنسان العطشان إذا أراد شرب الماء كان عليه أن يدنو من الماء ثم يبسط كفيه فيغترفه

TABATABAI:13:14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r8.claim: Those praying to others resemble the distant thirsty person: their invocation lacks substance and the invoked beings do not meet their needs.
TABATABAI:13:14/r8.anchor: ومثل من يدعو غير الله سبحانه مثل هذا الباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وليس له من الدعاء إلا صورته الخالية من المعنى

TABATABAI:13:14/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:14/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:14/r9.claim: The exception does not weaken the general denial: futile callers receive only the likeness of a response, so the parable intensifies the claim that they gain nothing at all.
TABATABAI:13:14/r9.anchor: ومن هنا يعلم أن هذا الاستثناء { إلا كباسط كفيه } الخ، لا ينتقض به عموم النفي في المستثنى منه

TABRISI:13:12-15/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r14.claim: Istijāba and ijāba both mean responding, but istijāba also conveys the act of requesting.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r14.anchor: والاستجابة والإجابة بمعنى غير أن في الاستجابة معنى الطلب

TABRISI:13:12-15/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r15.claim: The cited line, ‘no respondent answered him then,’ illustrates istijāba as response.

TABRISI:13:12-15/r25.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r25.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r25.claim: If kāf is a particle, it modifies an implied verbal noun: an answering like the answering of someone stretching his hands to water.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r25.anchor: والكاف من قوله كباسط كفيه يتعلق بصفة مصدر تقديره إلا استجابة كائنة كاستجابة باسط كفيه

TABRISI:13:12-15/r26.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r26.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r26.claim: If kāf is a noun, the estimate is ‘an answer like the answer of one who stretches his hands,’ with no pronoun in kāf.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r26.anchor: إذا كان اسما محضا فالتقدير إلا استجابة مثل استجابة باسط كفيه

TABRISI:13:12-15/r27.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r27.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r27.claim: The lām in li-yablugha is attached to bāsiṭ kafayhi.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r27.anchor: واللام في قوله ليبلغ فاه يتعلق بباسط كفيه

TABRISI:13:12-15/r28.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r28.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r28.claim: The clause may mean the water does not reach his mouth, his mouth does not reach the water, or the person with outstretched hands does not obtain the water.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r28.anchor: ما الماء ببالغ فاه وقيل ما فوه ببالغ الماء وقيل ما باسط كفيه إلى الماء

TABRISI:13:13-14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:13-14/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
TABRISI:13:13-14/r10.claim: One explanation identifies the true invocation as the declaration of divine unity, ‘There is no god but God.’
TABRISI:13:13-14/r10.anchor: أنها كلمة الإخلاص شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

TABRISI:13:13-14/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:13-14/r11.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:13:13-14/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan reasons that God is the Real, so calling on Him is the true invocation and whoever calls Him calls the Real.
TABRISI:13:13-14/r11.anchor: أن الله تعالى هو الحق فدعاؤه دعوة الحق ومن دعاه دعا الحق عن الحسن

TABRISI:13:13-14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:13-14/r12.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:13:13-14/r12.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī takes it as the invocation by which God is called upon in exclusive monotheism; God answers the sincere caller.
TABRISI:13:13-14/r12.anchor: أنها الدعوة التي يدعى بها الله على إخلاص التوحيد عن الجبائي

TABRISI:13:13-14/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:13-14/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:13-14/r13.claim: Those invoked beside God are the idols and other beings whom polytheists call on to meet their needs.
TABRISI:13:13-14/r13.anchor: أي والذين يدعوهم المشركون من دون الله لحاجاتهم من الأوثان وغيرها

TABRISI:13:13-14/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:13-14/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:13:13-14/r14.claim: The image compares idol worshippers hoping for benefit to someone reaching toward distant water that cannot reach his mouth; idols bring no benefit and answer no prayer.
TABRISI:13:13-14/r14.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله لكل من عبد غير الله ودعاه رجاء أن ينفعه

TABRISI:13:13-14/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:13-14/r15.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:13:13-14/r15.claim: Mujāhid pictures someone calling to water with his tongue and gesturing with his hand, but the water does not come.
TABRISI:13:13-14/r15.anchor: وقيل كباسط كفيه إلى الماء أي كالذي يدعو الماء بلسانه ويشير إليه بيده فلا يأتيه الماء عن مجاهد

TABRISI:13:13-14/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:13-14/r16.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:13:13-14/r16.claim: Al-Ḥasan pictures someone reaching for water who dies before it can reach his mouth.
TABRISI:13:13-14/r16.anchor: وقيل كالذي يبسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فمات قبل أن يبلغ الماء فاه عن الحسن

TABRISI:13:14-15/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة والبلخي وأبو مسلم
TABRISI:13:14-15/r1.claim: The Arabs use ‘like one grasping water’ for striving after something unattainable.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r1.anchor: وقيل إنه تمثيل العرب لمن يسعى فيما لا يدركه فيقول هو كالقابض على الماء

TABRISI:13:14-15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r2.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:13:14-15/r2.claim: An anonymous poet compares lost affection to someone holding water in his hand.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r2.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فأصبحت مما كان بيني وبينها

TABRISI:13:14-15/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r3.speaker: الشاعر الآخر
TABRISI:13:14-15/r3.claim: A second anonymous poem compares longing to water that the fingers cannot retain.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r3.anchor:
وقال الآخر:
فإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم

TABRISI:13:14-15/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:14-15/r4.claim: The unbelievers' invocation of idols leads away from truth and right guidance.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r4.anchor: أي ليس دعاؤهم الأصنام من دون الله إلا في ذهاب عن الحق والصواب

TABRISI:13:14-15/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:13:14-15/r5.claim: Another gloss says their invocation strays from the path of response and benefit.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r5.anchor: وقيل في ضلال عن طريق الإجابة والنفع

THALABI:v5p281/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p281/r1.claim: Those who call besides God are polytheists worshipping idols; the idols cannot answer their requests for benefit or protection from harm.
THALABI:v5p281/r1.anchor: والذين يدعون من دونه يعني المشركين الذين يعبدون الأصنام من دون الله لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء

THALABI:v5p281/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p281/r2.claim: The idolaters are like a thirsty person reaching and calling to water, gesturing with his hands, but the water never reaches him.
THALABI:v5p281/r2.anchor: إلا كما ينفع باسط كفيه إلى الماء من العطش يبسطه إياهما إليه يدعو الماء بلسانه ويشير إليه بيده

THALABI:v5p281/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p281/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, compares the polytheist to a thirsty man who sees his reflection in distant water and imagines he can reach it but cannot.
THALABI:v5p281/r3.anchor: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: هذا مثل لمشرك عبد مع الله غيره

THALABI:v5p281/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r4.speaker: عطية
THALABI:v5p281/r4.claim: ʿAṭiyya compares the idols to water a dying thirsty man reaches for but cannot bring to his mouth.
THALABI:v5p281/r4.anchor: عطية عنه يقول: مثل الأوثان التي يعبدون من دون الله كمثل رجل قد بلغه العطش

THALABI:v5p281/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r5.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p281/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says spread hands cannot hold or drink water; while the hands stay spread, water cannot reach the mouth, and grasping at water leaves nothing in one's hands.
THALABI:v5p281/r5.anchor: الضحاك عنه يقول: كما أن العطشان إذا يبسط كفيه إلى الماء لا ينفعه ما لم يحفظهما

THALABI:v5p281/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r6.speaker: ضابئ بن الحارث المزني
THALABI:v5p281/r6.claim: Ḍābiʾ ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī's verse compares longing to one cupping water whose fingers cannot bring it to him.
THALABI:v5p281/r6.anchor: قال ضابئ بن الحرث المزني: فإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم

THALABI:v5p281/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r7.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v5p281/r7.claim: An unnamed poet likewise compares lost affection to someone clutching water in his hand.
THALABI:v5p281/r7.anchor: وقال الشاعر: وأصبحت مما كان بيني وبينها

THALABI:v5p281/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p281/r8.claim: The disbelievers' appeal to their idols is wasted: the idols fail them when they need help.
THALABI:v5p281/r8.anchor: وما دعاء الكافرين أصنامهم إلا في ضلال يضل عنهم إذا احتاجوا إليه

THALABI:v5p281/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p281/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p281/r9.claim: Juybir transmits al-Ḍaḥḥāk's report from Ibn ʿAbbās that the disbelievers' prayers to their Lord are lost because their voices are veiled from God.
THALABI:v5p281/r9.anchor: جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: ما دعاء الكافرين ربهم إلا في ضلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r1.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس، الفراء، الزجاج، قتادة، وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r1.claim: Most commentators take “the true invocation” as the declaration of divine oneness and sincerity: “There is no god but God.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r1.anchor: روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس (¬6): {له دعوة الحق} قال: لا إله إلا الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r2.claim: On this reading, God’s creatures owe Him the true invocation; the genitive links two different expressions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r2.anchor: والمعنى على هذا: لله من خلقه الدعوة الحق، ولكن أضيفت الدعوة إلى الحق لما اختلف اللفظان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r3.claim: Another possible sense is “the invocation of the true religion.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: دعوة الدين الحق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r4.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the phrase as God, the Real.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r5.speaker: عطاء والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r5.claim: God is the one who calls people to affirm His oneness and acknowledge that He has no partner; the call is true because it summons people to worship and affirm Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r5.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء والضحاك: {له دعوة الحق} معناه: هو الذي دعا إلى توحيده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq suggests that a person who calls upon God in sincere monotheism will have the prayer answered.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وجائز أن يكون (دعوة الحق)، أنه من دعا الله موحدا استجيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r7.claim: The author prefers Abu Bakr’s reading: the singular “invocation” stands for the supplications of callers seeking an answer from God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r7.anchor: وهذا هو الوجه؛ وهو الأليق بما بعده من سياق الآية؛ لأنه ذكر أن الأصنام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r8.claim: These supplicants are in the right because they ask One who can answer, grant what is sought, and never disappoint a petitioner.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r8.anchor: لأنهم سألوا من لا يخيب سائله ويقدر على الإجابة، وإنالة المطلوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r9.speaker: جميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r9.claim: The beings invoked apart from God are the idols worshipped by the polytheists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r9.anchor: يعني الأصنام، يدعونها المشركون من دون الله، في قول جميع المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r10.claim: The verse speaks of idols with masculine forms used for rational beings because their worshippers attribute human-like rational qualities to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p321/r10.anchor: وعبر عنها كما يعبر عن المذكرين من العقلاء؛ لأنهم وصفوا أصنامهم بأوصاف الرجال العقلاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the callers receive no reward from the idols they invoke.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ليس لهم (¬2) ثواب، يعني للداعين إياه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r2.speaker: مجاهد وأبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r2.claim: Mujahid, chosen by Abu Ishaq, pictures someone calling water with his tongue and beckoning with his hand; it never comes, just as idols do not answer their worshippers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد (¬3): يدعو الماء بلسانه ويشير إليه بيده؛ فلا يأتيه أبدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r3.claim: The construction can be expanded as “except like the answering of one who stretches out his palms”; the genitive verbal noun is object-linked, with a governing noun omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r3.anchor: والتقدير: إلا كاستجابة باسط كفيه، ويكون المصدر مضافا إلى المفعول ثم حذف المضاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi pictures someone reaching toward water from far away while overlooking it, unable to reach it or bring it to his mouth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r4.anchor: قال: كماد يده إلى الماء من مكان بعيد وهو مشرف على ذلك الماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r5.speaker: عطاء والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r5.claim: Ata and al-Farra picture a thirsty person beside a well, reaching without a tool to draw water; the water cannot rise to his hand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r5.anchor: قال عطاء (¬1): كالرجل العطشان الجالس على شفير البئر يمد يده إلى البئر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r6.claim: The second picture resembles the first, but the first person calls distant water toward himself while the second reaches for it without a means to draw it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r6.anchor: إلا أن في الوجه الأول شبهوا بمن يدعو الماء البعيد إلى نفسه والماء لا يستجيب، وفي الوجه الثاني شبهوا بمن يمد يده إلى الماء البعيد ليناله من غير آلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد وابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd and Ibn Qutayba explain the image as an Arabic proverb for striving after something unattainable: water cannot be retained in a grasping hand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r7.anchor: الوجه الثالث: هو مذهب أبي عبيد (¬3) وابن قتيبة (¬4)، وهو أن العرب يضربون المثل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد وابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r8.claim: On this proverb reading, the idolaters gain nothing from their invocation, just as a person grasping water holds nothing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p323/r8.anchor: المعنى لا يصير في أيديهم إذا دعوهم إلا ما يصير في يدي من قبض على الماء ليبلغ فاه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses the poem’s verb as “to confront”; Ibn al-Anbari explains the phrase as collecting, carrying, or conveying the water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: تسقه: تجبه. وقال ابن الأنباري: يجمعه ويسقه يحمله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r2.claim: The cited Arabic line compares yearning for the absent beloved to trying to draw water with one’s fingertips, illustrating the futile grasping-water proverb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r2.anchor: فإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم ... كقابض ماء تستقيه أنامله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r3.claim: A second poem likewise likens lost affection to someone holding water in the hand, supporting the proverb’s sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r3.anchor: فأصبحت مما كان بيني وبينها ... من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the verse is elliptical: it means stretching one’s palms toward water to grasp it, or grasping it to bring it to one’s mouth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p324/r4.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: وهذا من الاختصار؛ لأن التقدير: إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليقبض عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r8.claim: God alone is rightly invoked by His creation; the true invocation is the declaration that there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r8.anchor: لله من خلقه الدعوة الحق، وهي كلمة التوحيد لا إله إلا الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r9.claim: Those who invoke besides God are the polytheists calling on idols.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r9.anchor: يعني: المشركين يدعون { من دونه } الأصنام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r10.claim: Their invocation is as futile as someone beckoning water to reach his mouth: the water cannot reach it by being called.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r10.anchor: إلا كما يستجاب للذي يبسط كفيه يشير إلى الماء، ويدعوه إلى فيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r11.claim: The disbelievers' worship of idols ends in ruin and is futile.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:13-14/r11.anchor: عبادتهم الأصنام { إلا في ضلال } هلاك وبطلان

QASHANI:13:13-14/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:13-14/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:13-14/r4.claim: The true, answered invocation belongs to the monotheist annihilated from self and abiding through God; pure religion likewise belongs only to Him.
QASHANI:13:13-14/r4.anchor: الدعوة الحقية التي ليست بالباطل له لا لغيره يدعو نفسه فيستجيب كما قال تعالى:

QASHANI:13:13-14/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:13-14/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:13-14/r5.claim: Self-standing petitioners address imagined, powerless objects and receive no response; their self-attributes veil their capacity, so their prayers are wasted.
QASHANI:13:13-14/r5.anchor: والدعاة القائمون بأنفسهم لا يدعون إلا من تصوروه ونحتوه في خيالهم فلا يستجاب لهم إلا كاستجابة الجماد

QASHANI:13:13-14/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:13-14/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:13-14/r6.claim: Alternatively, the Real's call belongs only to Him, and invocation of the Real is confined to His Essence rather than His names and attributes.
QASHANI:13:13-14/r6.anchor: أو دعوة المدعو الذي هو الحق هي الدعوة المختصة بذاته لا يدعى بها غيره من أسمائه وصفاته

QASHANI:13:13-14/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:13-14/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:13-14/r7.claim: Those invoking divine names or attributes apart from the Essence receive only a gesture-like answer, like someone calling water, because they are veiled.
QASHANI:13:13-14/r7.anchor: والواصفيون الذين يدعون أسماءه وصفاته من دون ذاته لا يستجيبهم المدعو إلا استجابة كاستجابة داعي الماء بالإشارة لكونهم محجوبين

ELMALILI:13:14/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r1.claim: One valid sense is that the call to truth—to the true deity and true religion—is a call to God alone; calls and propaganda made in another's name are false.
ELMALILI:13:14/r1.anchor: Hakka davet, insanları hak mâbuda, hak dine davet ancak O’na olan davettir. Allah’tan başkası nâmına yapılan davetler, propagandalar hep bâtıldır

ELMALILI:13:14/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r2.claim: Another valid sense is true supplication: prayer that is properly directed and answered belongs to invocation and worship of God alone.
ELMALILI:13:14/r2.anchor: hak dua, yani yerine masruf olan ve icâbet görecek olan dua, ancak Allah’a olan dua ve ibadettir

ELMALILI:13:14/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r3.claim: A third valid sense is the call to the true object sought: God alone first and directly shows and guides to truth.
ELMALILI:13:14/r3.anchor: hak matlûba davet, evvelen ve bizzat hakkı gösterip hidâyet edecek olan O’dur

ELMALILI:13:14/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r4.claim: The claim that God guides to truth is supported by Yunus 10:35; truth cannot be invited to without reliance on God's disclosure and guidance.
ELMALILI:13:14/r4.anchor: Allah’ın beyan ve irşâdına istinad etmeksizin hakka davet olunamaz

ELMALILI:13:14/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r5.claim: The invoked include deities promoted in their name, beings from whom needs are requested, and those called upon for aid or supplicated.
ELMALILI:13:14/r5.anchor: o kâfirlerin Allah’tan başka davet ettikleri veya dua edip durdukları yani namlarına propaganda yaptıkları, hâcet diledikleri mâbudlar, imdâda çağırdıkları

ELMALILI:13:14/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r6.claim: Those invoked cannot answer with anything or fulfill any request by their own power.
ELMALILI:13:14/r6.anchor: onlara hiçbir şeyle icâbet edemezler hiçbir dileklerini kendiliklerinden yerine getiremezler

ELMALILI:13:14/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r7.claim: The futile invocation resembles a thirsty person reaching both hands toward distant water, which cannot come into his mouth by itself.
ELMALILI:13:14/r7.anchor: ancak ağzına erişsin diye suya doğru iki avucunu açan susuz gibi boşuna avuç açmış olurlar

ELMALILI:13:14/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r8.claim: The prayers of unbelievers are wholly misguided.

ELMALILI:13:14/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r9.claim: It is obvious that inanimate idols cannot answer any prayer.
ELMALILI:13:14/r9.anchor: putların da hiçbir duaya cevap veremiyecekleri âşikârdır

ELMALILI:13:14/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r10.claim: Because the relative pronoun alladhina ordinarily denotes rational beings, restricting the referent to idols alone contradicts the apparent wording; rational beings worshipped beside God are included too.
ELMALILI:13:14/r10.anchor: وَٱلَّذِينَ mevsûlü zevi’l-ukūlde zâhir olduğu cihetle bunu yalnız asnâm ile tevil etmek hilâf-ı zâhirdir

ELMALILI:13:14/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r11.claim: Even rational beings made into objects of worship and supplication cannot answer any prayer, just like idols.
ELMALILI:13:14/r11.anchor: yalnız şuursuz putlar değil, Allah’ın mâdûnunda mâbud ittihaz edilen, yalvarılan zevi’l-ukūlün de putlar gibi hiçbir duaya icâbet edemeyecekleri

ELMALILI:13:14/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r12.claim: The wording seems puzzling for public cries, since people can hear them and sometimes respond in part.
ELMALILI:13:14/r12.anchor: duyduğu ve kısmen olsun icâbet de edebildiği dermeyan olunur

ELMALILI:13:14/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r13.claim: Limiting prayer to hidden, inward supplication would remove the objection, but the text gives no clue for that restriction and its monotheistic context weighs against it.
ELMALILI:13:14/r13.anchor: bu tahsis veya takyîde başkaca bir karîne olmadığı gibi, âyetin tevhîde müte‘allik olan siyâk u mezâkı da buna muhaliftir

ELMALILI:13:14/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r14.claim: The deeper truth is that no one can answer a supplication independently of God; all efficacy and connection among distinct beings depends on the One who governs them.
ELMALILI:13:14/r14.anchor: hakikatte Allah’tan kat‘-ı nazarla hiç kimsenin duaya icâbet etmesine imkân olmadığı anlatılmıştır

ELMALILI:13:14/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r15.claim: Distinct individual entities are separate precisely because each is its own thing; none is present in another, and they do not possess or interpenetrate one another's selfhood.
ELMALILI:13:14/r15.anchor: ve her biri diğer bir ayn olan mütemâyiz şeylerin yekdiğerine

ELMALILI:13:14/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r16.claim: The possibility that separate things affect and communicate with one another is a profound philosophical problem, including how matter affects matter, soul affects body, and body affects soul.
ELMALILI:13:14/r16.anchor: meselesi feylesofları hayrette bırakan en mu‘dil mes’ele-i felsefiye

ELMALILI:13:14/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r17.claim: Only by recourse to divine unity can interaction be explained; without the supreme One, the world would be disconnected things unable to relate to one another.
ELMALILI:13:14/r17.anchor: Şimşekler çakmaz, bulutlar inşâ edilmez, yağmurlar yağmaz, yıldırımlar düşmezdi

ELMALILI:13:14/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r18.claim: Natural processes and communication, from clouds, rain, and lightning to Zayd's cry reaching Amr, occur through the Lord of the worlds' command and management.
ELMALILI:13:14/r18.anchor: Bunlar olabiliyorsa hiç şüphe yok ki hep Rabbü’l-âlemîn’in emr ü tedbîriyle oluyor

ELMALILI:13:14/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r19.claim: A creature to whom one appeals is separate and distant, unable by itself to convey one's inner feeling or another thing to it, like a thirsty person reaching toward water from afar.
ELMALILI:13:14/r19.anchor: kendisinden ayrı ve uzaktır. Kendindeki bir hissi, bir şeyi diğerine nakletmesine imkân yoktur

ELMALILI:13:14/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r20.claim: Even breathing depends on God's permission; when death comes and the soul is taken by God's command, all the world's physicians cannot restore one breath to the dead.
ELMALILI:13:14/r20.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın izn ü müsaadesi olmayınca insan hava içinde nefes bile alamaz. Nitekim ecel gelip emr-i Rab olan rûh kabz olunduğu zaman, dünyanın tabibleri toplansa ölüye bir nefes veremezler

ELMALILI:13:14/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r21.claim: People and angels can hear cries only by God's permission, and can respond or help only by His leave; without it ears do not hear and hearts do not will.
ELMALILI:13:14/r21.anchor: Bir insanın feryâd ü ilticâsını diğer insanların veya melâikenin işitebilmesi sem‘ü ibsâra mâlik olan Allah teâlâ’nın emr ü müsaadesi sayesinde olduğu gibi, mümkin olan icâbet ve i‘ânede bulunabilmeleri de öyledir

ELMALILI:13:14/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r22.claim: Those besides God are independently unable to answer a needy person's prayer because they are separate from one another and cannot create anything in the first instance.
ELMALILI:13:14/r22.anchor: Allah’ın mâdûnundakiler nefislerinde birbirlerinden uzak oldukları

ELMALILI:13:14/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r23.claim: God is closer to each person than that person's own self; al-Baqara 2:186 says He is near and answers the supplication of the one who calls.
ELMALILI:13:14/r23.anchor: Allah teâlâ, herkese kendinden bile karîbdir

ELMALILI:13:14/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r24.claim: God hears even the most secret prayers, answers them, creates what is not already available to give, and joins separated things through His power and dominion.
ELMALILI:13:14/r24.anchor: En gizli duaları bile işitir, icâbet eder, vereceği mevcud değilse yaratır, hâlıktır. Birbirinden ayrı olan şeyleri kudretiyle, melekûtuyla yekdiğerine ulaştırır

ELMALILI:13:14/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:14/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:14/r25.claim: God can bring a person to water or bring water to the person's mouth; every relation among things is created by His act and command.
ELMALILI:13:14/r25.anchor: Dilerse insanı suyun yanına götürür, dilerse suyu onun ağzına getirir. Bütün eşyâ beynindeki irtibat ve münasebet hep O’nun halk u emriyledir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r1.claim: People seek refuge, worship, plead, and ask a stronger being for help; believers turn to God, while those rejecting true religion turn to false gods.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r1.anchor: İnsanoğlu daima kendisinden daha güçlü bir varlığa sığınma, tapınma, yalvarma ve yardım isteme ihtiyacında olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r2.claim: The image of reaching one's hands toward distant water shows that false gods will not answer their worshippers' pleas, just as water will not reach the person's mouth by itself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r2.anchor: Su almak için uzaktan avuçlarını suya uzatan kimsenin ağzına su kendiliğinden gelip onun ihtiyacına cevap vermeyeceği gibi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r3.claim: Only God is worthy of supplication: he is creator, whereas the idols and other beings treated as gods are created and cannot meet others' needs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r3.anchor: Zira tanrı diye taptıkları o varlıklar yaratan değil, yaratılmış varlıklardır; bu sebeple başkalarının ihtiyaçlarını karşılamaktan âcizdirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r4.claim: God is nearer than the jugular vein, knows hidden thoughts, hears open and secret prayers, meets needs, and can create what is absent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r4.anchor: kullarına şah damarından daha yakındır, kalplerinden geçenleri dahi bilir; onların açıktan ve gizli yakarışlarını işitir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r5.claim: Relying on false gods and asking them for help is baseless and futile; such prayers are wasted and miss their aim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:14/r5.anchor: bu tanrılara yapılan dualar boşa gitmiş, hedefini şaşırmış dualardır

QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r5.claim: The summons of truth shines in hearts through proof; whoever listens with understanding responds to the evidence of knowledge.
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r5.anchor: دواعي الحق تصير لائحة في القلوب من حيث البرهان فمن استمع إليها بسمع الفهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r6.claim: Satan’s promptings call a servant to sin by making it attractive; whoever listens with heedlessness answers the voice of error.
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r6.anchor: دواعي الشيطان التي تهتف بالعبد بتزيين المعاصي ، فمن أصغى إليها بسمع الغفلة استجاب لصوت الغي

QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r7.claim: The lower soul leads by the reins of self-interest; whoever leans toward its promptings falls into the humiliation of the veil.
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r7.anchor: ومعها دواعي النفس وهي قائدة للعبد بزمام الحظوظ ، فمن ركن إليها ولاحظها وقع في هوان الحجاب

QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r8.claim: The calls of truth arrive without an angelic intermediary, rational proof, or scholarly sign; when God makes a servant hear them, the servant necessarily responds to God through God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r8.anchor: ودواعي الحق تكون بلا واسطة ملك ، ولا بدلالة عقل ، ولا بإشارة علم

QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r9.claim: In the spiritual path, the soul’s promptings call to a kind of idolatry: seeing something of oneself, imagining claims for oneself, dwelling in separation, and being blind to the realities of union.
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r9.anchor: هواجس النفس ودواعيها تدعو - في الطريقة - إلى الشرك ، وذلك بشهود شيء منك ، وحسبان أمر لك

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r1.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r1.claim: The sermon compares the inviolability of Muslims’ blood, property, and honor to the sacred day, month, and place, lasting until the final meeting.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r1.anchor: قالوا في يوم حرام وشهر حرام وبلد حرام قال ألا فإن دماءكم وأموالكم وأعراضكم عليك حرام كحرمة يومكم هذا

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r2.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r2.claim: He forbids mutual wrongdoing and says a Muslim’s property is lawful only with its owner’s willing consent.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r2.anchor: اسمعوا مني تعيشوا ألا لا تظالموا ألا لا تظالموا ألا ألا تظالموا ألا انه لا يحل مال امريء مسلم إلا بطيب نفس منه

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r3.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r3.claim: All pre-Islamic blood claims are annulled, beginning with the blood claim for Rabīʿa ibn al-Ḥārith, killed by Hudhayl while nursed among Banū Layth.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r3.anchor: كان مسترضعا في بني ليث فقتلته هذيل

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r4.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r4.claim: All pre-Islamic usury is annulled, beginning with the debt of his uncle al-ʿAbbās; creditors may claim principal without wronging or being wronged.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r4.anchor: ألا وإن كل ربا كان في الجاهلية موضوع ألا وإن الله تعالى قضى أن أول ربا يوضع ربا عمي العباس لكم

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r5.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r5.claim: The calendar has returned to its original arrangement; the sermon cites the four sacred months and warns against wronging oneself in them.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r5.anchor: ألا وإن الزمان قد استدار كهيئته يوم خلق الله السموات والأرض

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r6.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r6.claim: He warns Muslims not to revert to killing one another as unbelievers; Satan has despaired of being worshipped by the praying but still seeks to stir conflict.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r6.anchor: ألا لا ترجعوا بعدي كفارا يضرب بعضكم رقاب بعض ألا وإن الشيطان قد يئس أن يعبده المصلون

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r7.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r7.claim: The sermon describes wives as entrusted dependents, sets reciprocal rights, forbids admitting unwanted guests to the marital bed, and prescribes admonition, bed separation, and non-injurious striking for feared nushūz.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r7.anchor: اتقوا الله في النساء فإنهن عندكم عوان لا يملكن لأنفسهن شيئا وإن لهن عليكم حقا

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r8.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r8.claim: Husbands owe wives customary provision and clothing; the marriage bond was taken under God’s trust and made lawful by God’s word.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r8.anchor: ولهن رزقهن وكسوتهن بالمعروف فإنما أخذتموهن بأمانة الله تعالى واستحللتم فروجهن بكلمة الله

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r9.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r9.claim: A person holding a trust must return it to its owner.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r9.anchor: ألا ومن كانت عنده أمانة فليؤدها إلى من ائتمنه عليها

BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r10.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r10.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r10.claim: He asks whether he has conveyed the message, instructs witnesses to inform absentees, and notes a later recipient may understand better than the hearer.
BAQILLANI:v1p130#2/r10.anchor: ثم بسط يده فقال ألا هل بلغت ألا هل بلغت ليبلغ الشاهد الغائب فرب مبلغ ابلغ من سامع

BAQILLANI:v1p123/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r1.claim: Literary experts can identify who follows another in diction, meaning, or both, and who adopts another’s style or merely resembles it.
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r1.anchor: يعلمون أيضا من له سمت بنفسه ورفت برأسه ومن يقتدي في الألفاظ أو في المعاني أو فيهما بغيره

BAQILLANI:v1p123/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r2.claim: Examples include al-Buḥturī’s borrowing from Abū Tammām, Abū Tammām’s borrowing from Abū Nuwās and Muslim, and poets who freely borrow from many sources.
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r2.anchor: إن البحتري يغير على أبي تمام إغارة ويأخذ منه صريحا وإشارة

BAQILLANI:v1p123/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r3.claim: Al-Mutanabbī’s denial of borrowing cannot fool experts, who point out every word or allusion he took from the Ṭāʾiyyayn.
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r3.anchor: وما الذي نفع المتنبي جحوده الأخذ وإنكاره معرفة الطائيين وأهل الصنعة يدلون على كل حرف أخذه منهما

BAQILLANI:v1p123/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r4.claim: Experts distinguish direct borrowing from resemblance of style, describing degrees of similarity from near-identical to as far apart as east and west.
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r4.anchor: فإذا تباينا وذهب أحدهما في غير مذهب صاحبه وسلك في غير جانبه قيل بينهما ما بين السماء والأرض

BAQILLANI:v1p123/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r5.claim: Because experts know literary genres and their limits in fine detail, they cannot miss speech that departs from every familiar form; confusion reflects deficient expertise.
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r5.anchor: فكيف يخفى عليهم الجنس الذي هو بين الناس متداول وهو قريب متناول من أمر يخرج عن أجناس كلامهم ويبعد عما هو في عرفهم

BAQILLANI:v1p123/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r6.claim: A modern claimant’s boast of surpassing al-Buḥturī, Abū Nuwās, or Muslim does not establish mastery; these poets differ greatly, and conceit does not diminish al-Buḥturī.
BAQILLANI:v1p123/r6.anchor: وهذا كما يشتبه على من يدعي الشعر

SULAMI:v1p329#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r1.claim: The most truthful calls are God's calls: answering the call of truth brings one to God, while answering the ego's calls leads to ruin.
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أصدق الدواعي دواعي الحق فمن أجاب داعي الحق بلغه إليه الحق ،

SULAMI:v1p329#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r2.claim: The caller of truth guides without Satan's or the ego's share; when its call is fulfilled, lights of truth leave the one called without doubt.
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد : داعي الحق ، داعي رشد لا يقع للشيطان فيه يد ولا يكون للنفس فيه نصيب

SULAMI:v1p329#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r3.claim: The caller of truth calls by means of the Real and toward the Real.
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : داعي الحق من يدعو بالحق إلى الحق .

SULAMI:v1p329#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r4.claim: Calls that summon through truth, toward truth, or to its path direct people to truth; whoever calls by himself calls only to himself and is astray.
SULAMI:v1p329#4/r4.anchor: قال جعفر : من دعا بنفسه فإلى نفسه دعا وهو الكفر والضلال وذلك محل الخيانة والإسقاط

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r1.claim: The Shammakh's line praises generosity: its raised banner is the glory sought by ʿAraba, who supplied the poet with provisions, rather than a military contest.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r1.anchor: إن الشعر كما تعلم لمدح الرجل بالجود والسخاء لأنه سأل الشماخ عما أقدمه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r2.claim: Reading the right hand as sheer physical strength would suit a context of force and battle better than this praise of generosity.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r2.anchor: ولو كان في ذكر البأس والبطش وحيث تراد القوة والشدة لكان حمل اليمين على صريح القوة أشبه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r3.claim: The right hand can signal deliberate care and seriousness because it is the honored, stronger hand and the one people begin with when pursuing an aim.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r3.anchor: وما زال الناس يقولون للرجل إذا أرادوا حثه على الأمر وأن يأخذ فيه بالجد أخرج يدك اليمنى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r4.claim: Al-Buhturi's line about his hand being in the patron's right hand supports this image of entrusted agency; Jurjani identifies the patron as Yunus ibn Bugha, favored by al-Muʿtazz.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r4.anchor: وإن يدي وقد أسندت أمري إليه اليوم في يدك اليمين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r5.claim: Jurjani adds Sulayman ibn Qutta's address to Banu Taym as a further contextual test in the discussion of right-hand imagery and intended action.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p311/r5.anchor: ولو أن هذا التأويل منهم كان في قول سليمان بن قته العدوى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p293/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p293/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p293/r1.claim: Eloquence cannot arise from bare word order: joining ضحك and خرج would add nothing unless their grammatical meanings and relations create a particular construction.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p293/r1.anchor: لأنه لو جاز أن يكون لمجرد ضم اللفظ إلى اللفظ تأثير في الفصاحة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p293/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p293/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p293/r2.claim: The claim that meanings do not increase while words do is coherent only if verbal increase means the qualities produced by observing grammatical meanings; bare sounds cannot increase in merit.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p293/r2.anchor: غير أن تجعل تزايد الألفاظ عبارة عن المزايا التي تحدث من توخي معاني النحو وأحكامه

RUMMANI:v1p82/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p82/r4.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p82/r4.claim: The image joins need for a benefit with grief at failing to obtain it, warning people to supplicate only God, who controls benefit and harm and loses nothing from anyone.
RUMMANI:v1p82/r4.anchor: والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء

DAMGHANI:v1p69/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r3.claim: The image of stretching one's hands to water means reaching from a distance.
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r3.anchor: إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r9.claim: Daʿwat al-ḥaqq means the testimony that there is no god but God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r9.anchor: والرابع عشر : لا إله إلا الله ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الرعد :

FARRA:v2p60/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p60/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p60/r3.claim: دعوة الحق means the testimony لا إله إلا الله.
FARRA:v2p60/r3.anchor: له دعوة الحق: [14] لا إله إلا الله

FARRA:v2p60/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p60/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p60/r4.claim: The idols cannot answer their callers, like a thirsty person reaching toward water without a way to draw it; the water still cannot reach his mouth.
FARRA:v2p60/r4.anchor: يعني الأصنام لا تجيب داعيها بشيء إلا كما ينال الظمآن المشرف على ماء

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r1.claim: The idolaters get nothing from the beings they call, just as water cannot be retained in a hand to carry it to the mouth.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r1.anchor: لا يصير في أيديهم منه إذا دعوهم إلا ما يصير في يدي من قبض على الماء ليبلغه فاه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r2.claim: Arabs use grasping water as an idiom for seeking what cannot be obtained; the cited anonymous poem gives the same image.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r2.anchor:
والعرب تقول لمن طلب ما لا يجد: هو كالقابض على الماء. قال الشاعر:
فإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم ... كقابض ماء لم تسقه أنامله (3)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r3.claim: In the poem, lam tasqihi means it did not carry the water; wasq means carrying or loading.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#2/r3.anchor: لم تسقه: أي لم تحمله، والوسق: الحمل.

MAJAZ:v1p325/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p325/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p325/r2.claim: This means those who call on someone other than God. Dūnahu is used like ʿanhu, “away from Him,” as the cited poet’s dūnī means ʿannī.
MAJAZ:v1p325/r2.anchor: «والذين يدعون من دونه» (14) مجازه: والذين يدعون غيره من دونه، أي يقصرون عنه

MAJAZ:v1p325/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p325/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p325/r3.claim: Lā yastajībūn means they do not answer; Kaʿb’s verse uses istajābah in this sense.
MAJAZ:v1p325/r3.anchor: «لا يستجيبون» (14) مجازه: لا يجيبون، وقال كعب: وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى

MAJAZ:v1p327/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p327/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p327/r1.claim: The comparison is to someone reaching for water with open hands, who cannot deliver it to his mouth or gather it with his fingers. The cited poets use the futile water-grasping image for something unobtainable.
MAJAZ:v1p327/r1.anchor: «إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه» (15) مجازه: إن الذي يبسط كفه ليقبض على الماء حتى يؤديه

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r1.claim: دعوة الحق may be an adjective-noun reversed in annexation, with the underlying phrase الدعوة الحق, as in one analysis of 12:109.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r1.anchor: من باب إضافة الموصوف إلى الصفة، والأصل: له الدعوة الحق كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers two senses: a call belonging to truth, opposite falsehood, like كلمة الحق; or a call to al-Ḥaqq, God, the true invoked one who hears and answers.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن تضاف الدعوة إلى الحق الذي هو نقيض الباطل،

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r3.claim: The Shaykh rejects the second sense because it would amount to لله دعوة الله, like لزيد دعوة زيد, which he considers an invalid construction.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا الوجه الثاني لا يظهر؛ لأن مآله إلى تقدير: لله دعوة الله

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r4.claim: Al-Samīn challenges the Shaykh's objection, asking how it follows from what al-Zamakhsharī actually said.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r4.anchor: قلت: وأين هذا مما قاله الزمخشري حتى يرد عليه به؟

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r5.claim: الذين may refer to the polytheists: they are the subject of يدعون, with idols omitted as its object; لا يستجيبون then refers to those idols, treated grammatically as rational.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يراد بالذين المشركون، فالواو في " يدعون " عائده، ومفعوله محذوف وهو الأصنام،

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that the worshippers' idols answer no more than water answers a person cupping hands toward it: inert water cannot hear or quench his thirst.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r6.anchor: قال معناه الزمخشري. ولما ذكر أبو البقاء قريبا من ذلك وقدر التقدير المذكور قال:

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ analyzes the analogy's verbal noun as annexed to its object, like 41:49 دعاء الخير, with water as the implicit subject; response is a metaphor for compliance.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r7.anchor: قال: " والمصدر في هذا التقدير مضاف إلى المفعول كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r8.claim: Alternatively, الذين refers to the idols, which are called rational either because the gods include rational beings and inanimate objects or because their worshippers treat them as rational.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالذين الأصنام، أي: والآلهة الذين يدعونهم من دون الله لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا استجابة،

SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r9.claim: On the idols-as-referent parse, the same failed water analogy applies; the text uses rational-plural agreement because of mixed objects of worship or the worshippers' treatment of idols as rational.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14/r9.anchor: وإنما جمعهم جمع العقلاء: إما للاختلاط؛ لأن الآلهة عقلاء وجماد، وإما لمعاملتهم إياها معاملة العقلاء

SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r1.speaker: اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r1.claim: Al-Yazidi transmits the address-form تدعون from Abu ʿAmr, which supports the second analysis; al-Zamakhshari mentions only that analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو " تدعون " بالخطاب وهو مقوية للوجه الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r2.claim: The lām in ليبلغ depends on باسط, and the implicit subject of ليبلغ is الماء.

SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r3.claim: One parsing takes هو as water and the suffix in ببالغه as mouth: the water does not reach into the mouth.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r3.anchor: أحدها: أنه ضمير الماء. والهاء في " ببالغه " للفم، أي: وما الماء ببالغ فيه.

SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r4.claim: A second parsing takes هو as mouth and the suffix as water; in this posture neither reaches the other, so either can be the grammatical subject.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r4.anchor: الثاني: أنه ضمير الفم، والهاء فيي " ببالغه " للماء، أي: وما الفم ببالغ الماء؛

SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r5.claim: A third parsing takes هو as the person stretching out his hands and the suffix as water: the person cannot reach the water.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r5.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون ضمير الباسط، والهاء في " ببالغه " للماء، أي: وما باسط كفيه إلى الماء ببالغ الماء.

SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r6.claim: The person stretching cannot be هو with an implicit subject of ببالغه and the suffix referring to water: the mismatched predicate requires an explicit subject, as in وما هو ببالغه الماء.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r6.anchor: لأنه حينئذ يكون من باب جريان الصفة على غير من هي] له، ومتى كان كذا لزم إبراز الفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r7.claim: The kāf in كباسط is either an adjective of an elided verbal noun or a circumstantial accusative describing that noun.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r7.anchor: والكاف في " كباسط ": إما نعت لمصدر محذوف، وإما حال من ذلك المصدر
