SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa says a particle kāf contains a pronoun returning to the omitted noun, whereas a nominal kāf does not.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " والكاف في " كباسط " إن جعلتها حرفا كان فيها ضمير

SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r9.claim: The author says most grammarians do not treat kāf as a noun; only al-Akhfash does, and the omitted described word is the estimated verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:13:14#2/r9.anchor: وكون الكاف اسما في الكلام لم يقل به الجمهور، بل الأخفش، ويعني بالموصوف ذلك المصدر

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r1.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r1.claim: A reported explanation identifies the true invocation as the testimony that there is no god but God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r1.anchor: جاء في التفسير: دعوة الحق شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r2.claim: Zajjāj also allows that the true invocation is a monotheist's prayer to God, which God answers.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r2.anchor: وجائز - والله أعلم - أن تكون دعوة الحق

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r3.claim: Idols answer no prayers; calling them is like a thirsty person asking water to reach his mouth, though water cannot respond or arrive.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r3.anchor: والماء لا يستجيب، فأعلم الله - عز وجل - أن دعاءهم الأصنام

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r4.claim: Another account pictures a person at a well's edge calling water from its bottom to his mouth; Zajjāj says the two explanations amount to the same thing.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء

ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n30/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n30/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n30/r1.claim: Asad allows "His is the call of truth" or true invocation to God alone; al-haqq names God as Ultimate Reality, so prayer is directed to Him and invoking anything else is futile.
ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n30/r1.anchor: expression da'wat al-haqq may be understood in the sense of "prayer directed towards Him who is the Ultimate Reality"

ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n31/r1.claim: Asad also renders the phrase as "side by side with God."

ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n32/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n32/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:14#n32/r1.claim: Asad explains that the literal expression is "his two palms."

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلىألفدرهمعرفاms158|و.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلىألفدرهمعرفاms158|و.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلىألفدرهمعرفاms158|و.claim: In دعوة الحق, the annexed verbal noun reiterates that the preceding expression الله أكبر is a true invocation.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلىألفدرهمعرفاms158|و.anchor: دعاء الحق ولكنه توكيد كأنه قال دعاء حقا

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r1.claim: The expressive atmosphere of al-Baqara favors more derivatives of itāʾ than Āl ʿImrān: the source counts 34 instances versus 19.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r1.anchor: فقد وردت في البقرة في أربعة وثلاثين موضعاً، ووردت في آل عمران في تسعة عشر موضعاً، فاقتضى الجو التعبيري في البقرة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The section frames those who demand punishment while relying on self-proclaimed deities as calling for their own doom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: those who are demanding God’s punishment while relying on their self-proclaimed deities are only calling for their own doom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: There are no divine associates; God alone is one.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: There are no associates of God. He is the one and only.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Calling any supposed deity is ultimately calling God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: So whenever a person calls on some deity He is actually calling on God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Calling God alone is beneficial and blessed because all authority and control belong to Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: What is implied is that only calling God is beneficial, consequential and blessed. This is because all authority and control are with Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Those who call on others receive no answer; these supposed deities hear nothing because they do not exist.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: All those who call others will never be answered by them. These deities or partners of God hear nothing because they do not even exist.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verse uses the mirage image to portray the futility of calling other deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The verse then cites the example of a mirage to portray this situation.

SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.claim: With a redundant preposition or لا, the exception follows the governed noun's syntactic case, as its substitute, rather than the preposition's surface case; the alternative wording with من is unavailable.
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.anchor: فلما كان كذلك حمله على الموضع فجعله بدلا منه كأنه قال ما

SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.claim: In ما أنت بشيء إلا شيء, Tamim has شيء in the nominative slot while Hijaz has it accusative; when the dialects coincide, Sibawayh favors the underlying syntactic case.
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.anchor: وبشئ في لغة أهل الحجاز في موضع منصوب

SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.claim: With لست بشيء إلا شيئا, the exception is accusative as though باء were absent; the cited line demonstrates باء before an accusative predicate.
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.anchor: وتقول لست بشئ إلا شيئا لا يعبأ به

SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.claim: In لا أحد فيها إلا عبد الله, the exception substitutes for the nominative مبتدأ slot; the construction answers هل من أحد, and a definite name cannot be directly coordinated with لا.
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.anchor: لا أحد فيها إلا عبد الله

SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.claim: In لا أحد رأيته إلا زيد, whether رأيته is the predicate or an adjective, the analysis makes the initial noun equivalent to لا أحد مرئي or لا أحد مرئيا.
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.anchor: رأيته إلا زيد إذا بنيت رأيته على الأول كأنك قلت

SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.claim: Hijazi ما and إن cannot be reordered like verbs because they are particles; a long construction can nevertheless make otherwise difficult word order acceptable.
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.anchor: يجز لأنهما ليسا بفعل فيحتمل قلبهما كما لم يجز فيهما التقديم والتأخير

SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.claim: أحد is normally confined to negation, so إن أحدا لا يقول ذاك is weak because negation follows an affirmative opening; it is tolerated when the whole sense is negative.
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.anchor: وهو ضعيف خبيث لأن أحدا لا يستعمل

SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.claim: After إن أحدا لا يقول, إلا زيدا can substitute for the initial noun under the negative sense, or إلا زيد can attach to يقول; the latter is weaker than constructions that begin with negation.
SIBAWAYH:لاعلىماعملفيالاسمولكنالاسموماعم.anchor: وإن شئت قلت إلا زيد فحملته

NASHR:v1p229/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p229/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p229/r5.claim: Starting again is always voluntary and must begin at a self-contained, meaningful point; its degrees of completeness and harm parallel the four categories of stopping.
NASHR:v1p229/r5.anchor: وأما الابتداء) فلا يكون إلا اختياريا ; لأنه ليس كالوقف تدعو إليه ضرورة فلا يجوز

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r1.claim: Qatāda explains “the true call” as the testimony that there is no god but God.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ له دعوة الحق ﴾ قال شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses “the true call” as “there is no god but God.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ دعوة الحق ﴾ قال لا إله إلا الله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r3.claim: Qatāda says the outstretched hands cannot bring water to the mouth while they remain extended and do not close around it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ﴾ قال كباسط يديه إلى الماء فليس ببالغ فاه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r4.claim: Qatāda says this is a parable for taking a god besides God: it will neither benefit nor protect its worshipper, who dies persisting in that practice.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p334/r4.anchor: قال هذا مثل ضربه الله لمن اتخذ من دون الله إلها أنه غير نافعه ولا يدفع عنه شيئا حتى يموت على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r1.claim: God alone has true supplication: it is rightly directed to Him, answered when made, and the genitive marks its exclusive relation to truth and its freedom from falsehood, error, and waste.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r1.anchor: أي الدعاء والتضرع الثابت الواقع في محله المجاب عند وقوعه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r2.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r2.claim: Al-Māwardī interprets this as supplication in fear, when people call only on God, and considers that reading closer to the verse's context; it is supported by the verse about those lost when people call on anyone but Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r2.anchor: وزعم الماوردي أن هذا أشبه بسياق الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r3.claim: Another reading takes دعوة as الدعاء, a request for response, and understands it as worship by inclusion; the genitive may be analyzed as attaching a described noun to its quality, so only God deserves worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r3.anchor: بمعنى الدعاء أي طلب الاقبال والمراد به العبادة للاشتمال

ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r4.claim: Some supply an omitted complement, الدعاء للعبادة: God alone rightly summons people to worship Him, and this is inseparable from the claim that worship belongs to Him alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r4.anchor: إن الدعوة بمعنى الدعاء ومتعلقها محذوف أي للعبادة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes الحق as God Himself: He is the true deity who hears the supplicant and answers.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن أن المراد من الحق هو الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r6.claim: The two principal readings serve the same polemic against associating rivals: whether الحق means truth opposed to falsehood or God's name, the construction marks His exclusive claim to supplication and worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r6.anchor: وبين صاحب الكشف حاصل الوجهين بأن الكلام مسوق لاختصاصه سبحانه بأن يدعى ويعبد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r7.claim: On the divine-name reading, replacing a pronoun with الظاهر الحق reinforces the lām and genitive, while God's true existence makes all else contingent on Him; alleged deities are false and cannot answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r7.anchor: ثم زيد ذلك باقامة الظاهر مقام المضمر معادا بوصف ينبىء عن اختصاصها به

ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r8.claim: The al-Kashf account answers Abū Ḥayyān's objection that the divine-name reading collapses into the awkward phrase الله دعوة الله, and makes al-Ṭībī's alternative gloss unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p123/r8.anchor: وبهذا سقط ما قاله أبو حيان في الاعتراض على الوجه الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r1.claim: If the occasion was the story of Arbad and ʿĀmir, the preceding description of God as severe in stratagem connects to their unseen destruction and the Prophet's answered prayer; otherwise it warns disputing unbelievers of divine punishment, an answered prayer against them, or their error in worshipping others.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r1.anchor: وجه تعلق هذه والجملة التي قبلها أعني

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r2.claim: A report about the Arbad and ʿĀmir episode says the Prophet prayed, “O God, restrain them from me as You will”; the author gives no grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r2.anchor: رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد روى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r3.claim: The same contextual argument could apply if the occasion of revelation was the story of a Jew or a tyrant.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r3.anchor: إن سبب النزول قصة اليهودي أو الجبار

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r4.claim: The relative phrase can refer to the idols that polytheists call upon; alternatively it refers to the polytheists, with the idols omitted as the object of يدعون because من دونه indicates worship beyond God.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r4.anchor: أي الأصنام الذين يدعونهم أي المشركون وحذف عائد الموصول في مثل ذلك كثير

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r5.speaker: البزدوي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r5.claim: Al-Bazdawī's reading through Abū ʿAmr has the second-person تاء, تدعون, supporting the view that the relative phrase denotes the idols addressed by the polytheists.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r5.anchor: قراءة البزدوي عن أبي عمرو ( تدعون ) بتاء الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r6.claim: The pronoun in لا يستجيبون refers to the relative under the first parsing and to its omitted object under the second; on either account the idols fail to answer the polytheists' requests.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r6.anchor: عليه عائد على ( الذين ) وعلى الثاني عائد على مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r7.claim: The idols give no response, just as water cannot move toward a person who stretches out his hands from afar and calls for it to reach his mouth without a vessel.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r7.anchor: إلا استجابة كاستجابة الماء لمن بسط كفيه إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān allows هو to refer to the mouth and the suffix in بالغه to water: in that posture the mouth cannot reach water, just as water cannot reach the mouth.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r8.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان كون ( هو ) ضمير الفم والهاء في ( بالغه ) ضمير الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r9.claim: Another parsing makes هو refer to the person extending his hands and the suffix in بالغه refer to water.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r9.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون الأول ضمير ( باسط ) والثاني ضمير الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r10.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r10.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects making هو refer to باسط and the suffix to the mouth: a participle predicated of someone other than its subject must expose its subject, requiring the wording وما هو ببالغه الماء.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124/r10.anchor: اسم الفاعل إذا جرى على غير من هو له لزم إبراز الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r1.claim: The usual reading depicts utter failure precisely when the supplicant most needs an answer; the composite simile portrays urgent seekers before insensible, powerless idols and is framed as mockery.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r1.anchor: والغرض كما قال بعض المدققين ففي الاستجابة على البت بتصوير

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r2.claim: The exception is an absolute exception from the broadest verbal category; استجابة is apparently an active verbal noun, as required by the overt verb, though it may be passive and annexed to باسط by the active/passive verbal-noun relation.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r2.anchor: فالاستثناء مفرغ من أعم عام المصدر كما أشرنا إليه والظاهر أن الاستجابة هناك مصدر من المبني للفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r3.claim: If hands are spread to drink rather than gesture or call, the comparison is to a person trying to take water with open fingers and gaining nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r3.anchor: وقد يراد من بسط الكفين إلى الماء بسطهما أي نشر أصابيعهما

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r4.claim: Some describe the likeness as the meagerness of the result, though Al-Alūsī says it amounts to none; this is an individual simile of a futile effort, like writing on water, not a compound intellectual comparison.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r4.anchor: وجعل بعضهم وجه الشبه قلة الجدوى ولعله أراد عدمها

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r5.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r5.claim: A report from ʿAlī compares the image to a thirsty person at a well's brink without a rope, unable to reach the bottom while the water cannot rise to him; Al-Alūsī says this returns to the first interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r5.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أن ذلك تشبيه بعطشان على شفير بئر بلا رشاء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda compares the futile appeal to clutching water, and says Arabs use the image for pursuing what cannot be attained; he cites two anonymous poems about grasping water by hand.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r6.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة أن ذلك تشبيه بالقابض على الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r7.claim: An anonymous poem likens a lost bond of affection to someone holding water in his hand, witnessing the idiom's futility.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r7.anchor: فأصبحت فيما كان بيني وبينها من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r8.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r8.claim: A second anonymous poem compares yearning for absent people to holding water that one's fingers cannot contain, illustrating the same futile pursuit.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r8.anchor: وإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم كقابض ماء لم تسعه أنامله

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r9.claim: Al-Alūsī says the water-clutching proverb is closer to the open-finger drinking interpretation, but باسط itself means spreading fingers, not clasping; a poem about a hand unable to close supports that distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r9.anchor: فان بسط الكف ظاهر في نشر الاصابيع ممدودة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r10.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r10.claim: The anonymous line تعود بسط الكف uses basting the palm for an open hand that cannot close, supporting the ordinary sense of باسط as fingers spread outward.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r10.anchor: تعود بسط الكف حتى لو أنه أراد انقباضا لم تطعه أنامله

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r11.speaker: بكير بن معروف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r11.claim: Al-Alūsī rejects as unreliable a report attributed to Bukayr ibn Maʿrūf that باسط means Cain, punished after killing his brother by being held over the sea just beyond reach of the water.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r11.anchor: عن بكير بن معروف من أنه قابيل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r12.speaker: قراء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r12.claim: A variant reads كباسطٍ كفيه with tanwīn, meaning like any person who spreads his two hands.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p124#2/r12.anchor: وقريء ( كباسط كفيه ) بالتنوين أي كشخص يبسط كفيه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r1.claim: The unbelievers' prayer is wasted, lost, and false; if it means prayer to idols, the claim follows from the previous verse and is repeated for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r1.anchor: أي في ضياع وخسار وباطل والمراد بهذا الدعاء إن كان دعاء آلهتهم فظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r2.claim: If the phrase means unbelievers' prayers to God, Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to say their voices are veiled from God so He does not hear them; Al-Alūsī limits this explanation to requests concerning the afterlife because some unbelievers' prayers, including Iblīs's, may be answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r2.anchor: من أن أصوات الكفار محجوبة عن الله تعالى فلا يسمع دعاؤهم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r3.claim: Another view allows the phrase to mean their prayers to God without restricting it to unanswered requests, despite the objection that some such prayers are granted.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p125/r3.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يراد دعاؤهم مطلقا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r1.claim: The true, sincere invocation belongs to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r1.anchor: {له دعوة الحق} أي: لله دعوة الصدق.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r2.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r2.claim: Ali explains the true invocation as monotheism.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r2.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: دعوة الحق التوحيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the true invocation as the testimony that there is no god but God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is sincere supplication, which can be directed only to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: الدعاء بالإخلاص، والدعاء الخالص لا يكون إلا لله عز وجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r5.claim: Those invoked besides God are idols worshipped instead of Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r5.anchor: {والذين يدعون من دونه} أي: يعبدون الأصنام من دون الله تعالى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r6.claim: The idols answer no request for benefit or for warding off harm.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r6.anchor: {لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء} أي: لا يجيبونهم بشيء يريدونه من نفع أو دفع ضر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r7.claim: Cupped hands cannot hold water or bring it to the mouth; idol worshippers likewise gain nothing from powerless idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r7.anchor: لا يكون في يده شيء، ولا يبلغ إلى فيه منه شيء، كذلك الذي يدعو الأصنام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r8.claim: Mujahid likens the worshipper to a thirsty person who sees distant water, gestures and calls, but never reaches it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه كالرجل العطشان الذي يرى الماء من بعيد، فهو يشير بكفه إلى الماء، ويدعوه بلسانه، فلا يأتيه أبدا، هذا معنى قول مجاهد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r9.speaker: علي وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r9.claim: Ali and Ata compare the idolater to a thirsty person at a well who cannot reach its water, and whose call cannot make water rise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r9.anchor: ومثله عن علي وعطاء: كالعطشان الجالس على شفير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says hands spread in water do not help a thirsty person unless he scoops it; this depicts the disbelievers' frustration.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p305#2/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: كالعطشان إذا بسط كفيه في الماء لا ينفعه ذلك ما لم يغرف بهما الماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306/r1.claim: The disbelievers' invocation is directed to their idols, which abandon them when needed; the verse echoes the statement that their fabrications disappear.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306/r1.anchor: {وما دعاء الكافرين} أصنامهم، {إلا في ضلال} يضل عنهم إذا احتاجوا إليه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas explaining this as disbelievers' prayer to their Lord being lost because their voices are screened from God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس: وما دعاء الكافرين ربهم إلا في ضلال لأن أصواتهم محجوبة عن الله تعالى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r1.claim: One reading takes this as the true invocation: God alone deserves worship and calling upon Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r1.anchor: الدعاء الحق فإنه الذي يحق أن يعبد ويدعى إلى عبادته دون غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r2.claim: An alternative takes it as the answered invocation, supported by what follows about response to prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r2.anchor: أو له الدعوة المجابة فإن من دعاه أجابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r3.claim: On either reading, حق means the opposite of falsehood; the genitive construction reflects association, or means the invocation of the One who is true.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r3.anchor: و { الحق } على الوجهين ما يناقض الباطل

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes الحق as God Himself, making every invocation directed to Him an invocation of truth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r4.anchor: وقيل { الحق } هو الله تعالى وكل دعاء إليه دعوة الحق

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r5.claim: If the passage concerns Arbad and Amir, their destruction unseen by them is God's answer to the Messenger's prayer or proof that he is truthful.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r5.anchor: إن كانت الآية في أربد وعامر أن إهلاكهما من حيث لم يشعرا به محال من الله إجابة لدعوة رسوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r6.claim: On a general reading, the passage threatens unbelievers arguing with the Messenger with destruction or an answered prayer against them, and may also expose their error and unsound judgment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r6.anchor: وإن كانت عامة فالمراد وعيد الكفرة على مجادلة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r7.claim: The phrase can mean idols called upon by polytheists, with the resumptive pronoun omitted, or polytheists calling idols, with the object omitted because context supplies it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r8.claim: Their gods answer no request; the exception compares them to someone stretching both hands toward water and asking it to reach his mouth, since an idol is insensible and powerless.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r8.anchor: إلا استجابة كاستجابة من بسط كفيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r9.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r9.claim: An alternative comparison is to someone who hopes to scoop water to drink but merely opens his hands toward it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r9.anchor: وقيل شبهوا في قلة جدوى دعائهم لها بمن أراد

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r10.claim: The phrase is also read with second-person تدعون and with باسط carrying tanwīn.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:14/r11.claim: The invocation of unbelievers comes to nothing: it is loss and falsehood.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r1.claim: After mentioning signs of divine perfection and that most believers still associate partners, Biqaʿi explains their error by God's lack of any equal; he recalls 12:105–106.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r1.anchor: شرع يبين ضلالهم في اشتراكهم المشار إليه في قوله : { وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون }

BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r2.claim: Only God has the true invocation: if called, He hears and answers as He wills; alternatively, His command clarifies truth, or His decree makes the called submit.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r2.anchor: إن دعاه أحد سمعه فأجابه - إن شاء - بما يشاء , وإن دعا هو أحدا دعوة أمر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r3.claim: Those who call on others beside God are the unbelievers, and the objects they invoke cannot answer them at all.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r3.anchor: أي يدعو الكافرون , وبين سفول رتبتهم بقوله : { من دونه } أي الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r4.claim: Istijābah means following a caller in the request in a way that accords with the caller’s will.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r4.anchor: والاستجابة : متابعة الداعي فيما دعا إليه بموافقة إرادته

BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r5.claim: Their futile invocation resembles someone stretching both hands toward water that cannot sense a call or reach his mouth; idols are just as unresponsive.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r5.anchor: كما أن الماء جماد لا يحس بدعوة هذا فلا يجيبه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r6.claim: Kaff is the gripping part of the hand, named from gathering its fingertips; the preposition ilā indicates that his hands do not actually reach the water.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r6.anchor: تثنية كف , وهو موضع القبض باليد , وأصله من كفه - إذا جمع أطرافه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r7.claim: The water will not reach the man’s mouth, just as the false gods do not respond to those invoking them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r7.anchor: دون أن يصل كفاه إلى الماء - بما يدل عليه التعدية ب ( إلى )

BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p134/r8.claim: The verse generalizes from their particular invocation by naming unbelievers as a class whose calls are always futile; idols neither harm nor benefit, and God does not answer those who neglect monotheism.

DURR-FULL:v4p628/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r2.claim: Ali interprets the true call as divine oneness: «There is no god but God».
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {له دعوة الحق} قال: التوحيد لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v4p628/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the true call as the testimony that there is no god but God.
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {له دعوة الحق} قال: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v4p628/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the confession belongs to God alone; no one else should be called a tribal deity.
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r4.anchor: عن ابن زيد - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {له دعوة الحق} قال: لا إله إلا الله ليست تنبغي لأحد غيره

DURR-FULL:v4p628/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r5.claim: Ali compares futile invocation to a thirsty man reaching toward a well and hoping water will rise to him.
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r5.anchor: عن علي - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {الا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه} قال: كالرجل العطشان يمد يده إلى البئر

DURR-FULL:v4p628/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r6.claim: Mujahid pictures someone calling to water and pointing at it; it never comes, just as those invoked besides God do not answer.
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {كباسط كفيه إلى الماء} قال: يدعو الماء بلسانه ويشير إليه بيده فلا يأتيه أبدا

DURR-FULL:v4p628/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r7.claim: Qatada says the water remains unreachable until the thirsty man’s neck tears; likewise idols bring no good or protection from harm.
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r7.anchor: عن قتادة - رضي الله عنه - {والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه} وليس ببالغه حتى يتمزع عنقه

DURR-FULL:v4p628/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r8.claim: Qatada says the idol or stone cannot answer, bring good, or avert harm before death.
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r8.anchor: هذا الوثن وهذا الحجر لا يستجيب له بشيء في الدنيا ولا يسوق إليه خيرا ولا يدفع عنه سوءا حتى يأتيه الموت

DURR-FULL:v4p628/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r9.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r9.claim: Aṭaʾ pictures a man reaching from a well’s rim to its bottom: his hands cannot reach the water and it does not leap to him.
DURR-FULL:v4p628/r9.anchor: عن عطاء - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {والذين يدعون من دونه} الآية قال: الرجل يقعد على شفة البئر فيبسط كفيه

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r1.speaker: بكير بن معروف
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r1.claim: Bukayr reports that Cain was suspended by his forelock over the sea, close enough to feel water but unable to reach it; summer brought scorching heat and winter snow.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r1.anchor: عن بكير بن معروف - رضي الله عنه - قال: لما قتل قابيل أخاه جعله الله بناصيته في البحر ليس بينه وبين الماء إلا أصبع

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas compares a polytheist invoking another deity with a thirsty man who sees his reflection in distant water but cannot reach it.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه} قال: هذا مثل المشرك الذي عبد مع الله غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r1.claim: This conclusion follows proofs of God’s uniqueness in first and second creation, complete power, and universal knowledge: only the possessor of these attributes is truly worshipped, and worship of others is error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r1.anchor: التي هي براهين الانفراد بالخلق الأول ، ثم الخلق الثاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r2.claim: دعوة is a request that someone turn toward the caller, often for aid or favor; when directed to God it means seeking deliverance or blessing, since literal turning toward Him is impossible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r2.anchor: والدعوة : طلب الإقبال ، وكثر إطلاقها على طلب الإقبال للنجدة أو للبذل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r3.claim: The genitive may mean a true, deserved invocation, or an invocation originating in truth—monotheism—as opposed to idol worship originating in falsehood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r3.anchor: وإضافة الدعوة إلى الحق إما من إضافة الموصوف إلى الصفة إن كان الحق بمعنى مصادفة الواقع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r4.claim: The lām marks figurative ownership as entitlement, and placing the prepositional phrase first restricts the right of true invocation to God alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r4.anchor: واللام للملك المجازي وهو الاستحقاق . وتقديم الجار والمجرور على المبتدإ لإفادة التخصيص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r5.claim: The clause about those invoked apart from God states the implication of the preceding restriction; it is conjoined because its elaboration and illustration exceed a bare explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r5.anchor: وقد صرح بمفهوم جملة القصر بجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r6.claim: The relative expression refers to idols, the subject of يدعون is the polytheists, and an object pronoun is omitted: “those who call them apart from Him.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r6.anchor: واسم الموصول صادق على الأصنام . وضمير يدعون للمشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r7.claim: Idols receive the rational plural pronoun يستجيبون by conventional Arab usage, which treats idols as if they were rational agents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p107#2/r7.anchor: وأجري على الأصنام ضمير العقلاء في قوله : { لا يستجيبون } مجازاة للاستعمال الشائع في كلام العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r1.claim: استجابة means answering a caller’s cry or invocation; the added sīn and tāʾ intensify the action.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r1.anchor: والاستجابة : إجابة نداء المنادي ودعوة الداعي ، فالسين والتاء لقوة الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r2.claim: The bāʾ makes يستجيبون take the thing answered with; when fulfillment of the desired outcome is meant, the verb can stand without it, as at 12:34.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r2.anchor: والباء في بشيء لتعدية { يستجيبون } لأن فعل الإجابة يتعدى إلى الشيء المجاب به بالباء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r3.claim: The bāʾ makes the denial extend to any reply at all, even a promise of a gift or an excuse; idols cannot do even that, much less anything greater.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r3.anchor: فلما أريد هنا نفي إجداء دعائهم الأصنام جعل نفي الإجابة متعديا بالباء إلى انتفاء أقل ما يجيب به المسؤول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r4.claim: The indefinite شيء belittles the response and means the smallest verbal reply one could give.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r4.anchor: وتنكير شيء للتحقير . والمراد أقل ما يجاب به من الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r5.claim: The exception ranges over the whole scene of caller, invoked, invocation, and response; whether phrased as a supplicant or a state, the simile ironically confirms that no response occurs in other circumstances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r5.anchor: والاستثناء في إلا كباسط كفيه } من عموم أحوال الداعين والمستجيبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r6.claim: The person stretches open, uncupped hands to scoop water, but it cannot stay in them; this depicts an effort that wastes its desired object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r6.anchor: والمراد ب ( باسط كفيه ) من يغترف ماء بكفين مبسوطتين غير مقبوضتين إذ الماء لايستقر فيهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda cites a poem comparing futile love to someone grasping water by hand, supporting the image of an unattainable object; no grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r7.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة : فأصبحت فيما كان بيني وبينها من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r8.claim: إلى marks the endpoint because باسط already implies stretching the open hands toward the water.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r8.anchor: و { إلى } للانتهاء لدلالة { باسط } على أنه مد إلى الماء كفيه مبسوطتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r9.claim: The lām in ليبلغ marks purpose; the subject pronoun of يبلغ refers to water, while هو and the suffix in بالغه refer to the mouth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r9.anchor: واللام في { ليبلغ } للعلة . وضمير { يبلغ } عائد إلى الماء . وكذلك ضمير { هو } والضمير المضاف إليه في ( بالغه ) للفم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r10.claim: The parable compares polytheists’ calls to idols for benefit, and the idols’ failure to answer, to a thirsty person whose open-handed effort cannot bring water to his mouth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p108/r10.anchor: شبه حال المشركين في دعائهم الأصنام وجلب نفعهم وعدم استجابة الأصنام لهم بشيء بحال الظمآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p109/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p109/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p109/r1.claim: This clause is conjoined to the statement about those invoked, covering both the invoked’s inability and the caller’s failure: the earlier simile implies the caller’s disappointment, while this clause states it explicitly and summarizes the argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p109/r1.anchor: وجملة { وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال } عطف على جملة { والذين يدعون من دونه } لاستيعاب حال المدعو وحال الداعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p109/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p109/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p109/r3.claim: فِي is a figurative locative expressing entrenchment in the quality: their invocation is utterly lost.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p109/r3.anchor: و { في } للظرفية المجازية للدلالة على التمكن في الوصف ، أي إلا ضائع ضياعا شديدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r1.claim: Arab proverbs originally evoked eloquent descriptions of symbolic situations; as usage continued, people forgot the situation and retained the proverb’s point, while the Qur’an develops its parables explicitly and inventively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r1.anchor: لما تداولتها الألسن في الاستعمال وطال عليها الأمد نسيت الأحوال التي وردت فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s constructed parables include disbelievers’ deeds as storm-driven ash, the associator falling from heaven, a mirage, and the futile water-seeker in this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r2.anchor: فقد أوضح الأمثال وأبدع تركيبها كقوله تعالى ) مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r3.claim: The Qur’an uses varied styles; suras have distinctive tones, and some are built on recurring fawasil while others are not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r3.anchor: فإن بعضها بني على فواصل وبعضها ليس كذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r4.claim: Some suras open ceremonially with praise, an address to believers, or alif-lam-mim and a declaration of the Book, like introductions in literary composition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r4.anchor: منها ما افتتح بالاحتفال كالحمد ، ويا أيها الذين آمنوا ، وآلم ذلك الكتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r5.claim: Other suras begin by attacking their subject immediately, as in the opening of Muhammad and the declaration at the start of al-Tawba.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r5.anchor: ومنها ما افتتح بالهجوم على الغرض من أول الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r6.claim: The Qur’an’s concision can let most verses yield several meanings consistent with their wording; compatible possibilities may coexist, while even exclusive possibilities can prompt the reminder’s intended response.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r6.anchor: صلوحية معظم آياته لأن تؤخذ منها معان متعددة كلها تصلح لها العبارة باحتمالات لا ينافيها اللفظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s layered meanings would take many times its length to express without this concision, and its subtle signs may exceed a scholar’s notice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r7.anchor: ولولا إيجاز القرآن لكان أداء ما يتضمنه من المعاني في أضعاف مقدار القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r8.claim: Qur’anic ellipsis always has a clue in the wording or context, while also allowing much meaning in few words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r8.anchor: ولكنك لا تعثر على حذف يخلو الكلام من دليل عليه من لفظ أو سياق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls deletion and abbreviation a characteristic method of revelation; Ibn Ashur cites a Roman bishop’s remark that a verse gathers what was revealed to Jesus about this life and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r9.anchor: قال في الكشاف في سورة المدثر الحذف والاختصار هو نهج التنزيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r10.speaker: أحد بطارقة الروم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r10.claim: A Roman bishop told Umar that the verse about obeying God and His Messenger gathers what was revealed to Jesus concerning worldly and afterlife matters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r10.anchor: قال بعض بطارقة الروم لعمر بن الخطاب لما سمع قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r11.claim: The revelation to Moses’ mother compresses two commands, two prohibitions, and two glad tidings into one passage.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r12.claim: The Qur’anic phrase about life through retaliation is more concise than the familiar Arab saying that killing most effectively prevents killing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r12.anchor: مقابلا أوجز كلام عرف عندهم وهو القتل أنفى للقتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r13.claim: Al-Sakkaki extensively analyzes the eloquence of the earth-and-heaven command, while al-Baqillani treats distinctive features of al-Naml.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r13.anchor: بسط السكاكي في المفتاح آخر قسم البيان نموذجا مما اشتملت عليه هذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r16.claim: Another concise construction omits a governing noun, as in the declaration that righteousness is whoever believes in God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r16.anchor: ومنه حذف المضاف كثيرا كقوله تعالى ) ولكن البر من آمن بالله (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r17.claim: An omitted clause can be supplied from context: after God tells Moses to strike the sea, the text leaves implicit that Moses struck it before it parted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r17.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى ) وأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر فانفلق (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r18.claim: A text may state a general rule while intending a particular case, yielding the general rule, the specific ruling, and the benefit of identifying that case as part of the general class.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p121/r18.anchor: ومن ذلك الإخبار عن أمر خاص بخبر يعمه وغيره لتحصل فوائد : فائدة الحكم العام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r1.claim: The pronoun ‘to Him’ refers to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r1.anchor: الضمير في له عائد على اسم الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the true call as ‘There is no god but God’; Ibn Atiyya extends this to any part of religious law with the same meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: دعوة الحق: لا إله إلا الله. قال القاضي أبو محمد: وما كان من الشريعة في معناها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r3.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says the true call is monotheism.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: دعوة الحق: التوحيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r4.claim: The phrase may also mean that God alone receives the servants’ true invocation, whereas invocation of idols is false.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r4.anchor: ويصح أن يكون معناها له دعوة العباد بالحق، ودعاء غيره من الأوثان باطل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r5.claim: ‘Those whom they call’ refers to objects worshipped apart from God; ‘they call’ refers to Quraysh and other Arabs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r5.anchor: وقوله: والذين يراد به ما عبد من دون الله، والضمير في يدعون لكفار قريش وغيرهم من العرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r6.speaker: اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r6.claim: Al-Yazidi reports that Abu Amr read ‘you call’ with a second-person tāʾ; yastajibūn means ‘they answer,’ as supported by poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r6.anchor: وروى اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء: «تدعون من دونه» بالتاء من فوق، ويستجيبون بمعنى يجيبون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r7.claim: Idols do not answer anything unbelievers ask for their needs and benefits; the cited poet uses the verb for answering a call.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r7.anchor: وداع دعا: يا من يجيب إلى الندا ... فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r8.claim: Futile invocation is like a person beckoning water toward his mouth: it never reaches him, just as idols cannot answer or benefit their callers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r8.anchor: ثم مثل تعالى مثالا لإجابتهم بالذي يبسط كفيه نحو الماء ويشير إليه بالإقبال إلى فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r9.claim: ‘It’ may be water and ‘reaching it’ the mouth, or ‘it’ may be the mouth and the pronoun water, since the mouth cannot reach water in that posture.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r9.anchor: وقوله: هو يراد به الماء، وهو البالغ، والضمير في «بالغه» للفم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r10.claim: The unbelievers’ invocation ends in loss and misguidance and brings no benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r10.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى عن دعاء الكافرين أنه في انتلاف وضلال لا يفيد فيه شيئا ولا يغنيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r1.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, and most interpreters say the true call is the declaration of God's oneness, lā ilāha illā Allāh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنها كلمة التوحيد وهي لا إله إلا الله قاله علي وابن عباس والجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r2.claim: On this reading, the call is ascribed to truth because the two words differ in form while referring to the same reality.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r2.anchor: فالمعنى له من خلقه الدعوة الحق فأضيفت الدعوة إلى الحق لاختلاف اللفظين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God is the Real, so whoever calls upon Him calls upon the Real.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r3.anchor: والثاني أن الله عز وجل هو الحق فمن دعاه دعا الحق قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r4.claim: Those invoked besides God are idols worshipped as deities; Abū ʿUbayda glosses the phrase as those who invoke someone other than Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r4.anchor: يعني الأصنام يدعونها آلهة قال أبو عبيدة المعنى والذين يدعون غيره من دونه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r5.claim: The phrase means that the idols do not answer their callers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى ( لا يستجيبون لهم ) أي لا يجيبونهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r6.speaker: علي وعطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r6.claim: ʿAlī and ʿAṭāʾ picture a thirsty person extending his hand toward a well, unable to make its water rise to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r6.anchor: أحدها أنه العطشان يمد يده إلى البئر ليرتفع الماء إليه وما هو ببالغه قاله علي عليه السلام وعطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r7.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r7.claim: Al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās describes a thirsty man whose hands are already in the water but who cannot lift it to himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه الرجل العطشان قد وضع كفيه في الماء وهو لا يرفعهما رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r8.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r8.claim: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās pictures a thirsty man seeing his reflection far off in water and unable to reach it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r8.anchor: والثالث أنه العطشان يرى خياله في الماء من بعيد فهو يريد أن يتناوله فلا يقدر عليه رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r9.claim: Mujāhid says the man calls to the water and gestures toward it, but it never comes to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r9.anchor: والرابع أنه الرجل يدعو الماءبلسانه ويشير إليه بيده فلا يأتيه أبدا قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn Qutayba say the man tries to cup water in his hands and bring it to his mouth, which cannot work.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r10.anchor: والخامس أنه الباسط كفيه ليقبض على الماء حتى يؤديه إلى فيه لا يتم له ذلك والعرب تقول من طلب مالا يجد فهو القابض على الماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r11.claim: An Arabic maxim compares seeking the unattainable to grasping water; a cited poem uses this image, with wasq meaning a load or carrying.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r11.anchor: وأنشدوا وإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم كقابض ماء لم تسقه أنامله أي لم تحمله والوسق الحمل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r12.claim: A second anonymous poem compares the lost bond between two people to someone trying to grasp water by hand.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p317/r12.anchor: وقال آخر فأصبحت مما كان بيني وبينها من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p318/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p318/r1.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p318/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās says the unbelievers' prayers to their Lord are futile because their voices are veiled from God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p318/r1.anchor: أحدهما وما دعاء الكافرين ربهم إلى في ضلال لأن أصواتهم محجوبة عن الله رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p318/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p318/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p318/r2.claim: Muqātil interprets the unbelievers' invocation as worship of idols, which is loss and falsehood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p318/r2.anchor: والثاني وما عبادة الكافرين الأصنام إلا في خسران وباطل قاله مقاتل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r1.claim: Ali explains the true invocation as tawhid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r1.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه: {له دعوة الحق} قال: التوحيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، مالك عن محمد بن المنكدر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Malik, transmitting from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, identify the true invocation as There is no god but God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وقتادة، ومالك عن محمد بن المنكدر: {له دعوة الحق}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r3.claim: Those invoked apart from God are the idols worshipped alongside Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r3.anchor: أي: ومثل الذين يعبدون آلهة غير الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r4.claim: Ali likens them to someone reaching for water from the edge of a well but never managing to grasp it or bring it to his mouth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r4.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب: كمثل الذي يتناول الماء من طرف البئر بيده، وهو لا يناله أبدا بيده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says the person calls the water with his tongue and gestures to it with his hand, but it never comes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {كباسط كفيه} يدعو الماء بلسانه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r6.claim: An alternative takes the image as someone clutching water, unable to hold or control any of it; an anonymous poet uses this image for unfulfilled longing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: المراد كقابض يده على الماء، فإنه لا يحكم منه على شيء، كما قال الشاعر:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r7.speaker: الآخر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r7.claim: A second anonymous poet compares a lost relationship to someone grasping water in his hand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r7.anchor: وقال الآخر: (6) فأصبحت مما كان بيني وبينها … من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r8.claim: Whether the water is grasped or approached from afar, it cannot reach the mouth; likewise idol worshippers gain no benefit from their deities in this life or the next, and disbelievers’ prayers are futile.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p445#2/r8.anchor: ومعنى الكلام: أن هذا الذي يبسط يده إلى الماء، إما قابضا وإما متناولا له من بعد

JISHUMI:v5p3766/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r3.claim: Istijaba and ijaba both mean answering, but istijaba also carries the sense of seeking or requesting.
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r3.anchor: غير أن في الاستجابة معنى الطلب

JISHUMI:v5p3766/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r4.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r4.claim: The poet's use of يستجبه witnesses the sense of responding to a call for help.
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر: وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندا ... فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب

JISHUMI:v5p3766/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r10.claim: The genitive construction دعوة الحق is used although الدعوة itself is الحق, because the two nouns differ, like مسجد الجامع and the cited phrase ولدار الآخرة.
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r10.anchor: أضيف الدعوة إلى الحق، وإن كانت الدعوة هي الحق؛ لاختلاف الاسمين، كما يقال: مسجد الجامع، ومنه: (ولدار الآخرة).

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd identify دعوة الحق as the testimony of divine oneness, there is no god but Allah.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r1.anchor: قيل: كلمة الإخلاص شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r2.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r2.claim: Al-Hasan explains that Allah is the Real, so whoever calls on Him has called on truth.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r2.anchor: وقيل: الله الحق من دعاه دعا الحق، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r3.claim: Another explanation says that whoever calls on God calls on a living, powerful, hearing, knowing, seeing being, so the invocation is true and not lost.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r3.anchor: وقيل: من دعاه فقد دعا حيا قادرا سميعا، عالما، بصيرا، فيكون دعاؤه حقا، ولا يذهب باطلا

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r4.claim: Another gloss is that God's worship is the truth because no other being deserves worship.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r4.anchor: وقيل: عبادته الحق؛ لأن غيره لا يستحق العبادة

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r5.claim: Another interpretation is an invocation made with a sound expectation of an answer, and such a prayer is heard and answered.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r5.anchor: وقيل: هي الدعاء الذي يقع على وجه يؤمل فيه الإجابة؛ لأن الدعوة على هذا الوجه تكون مسموعة مستجابة

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r6.claim: A further gloss is the call to the truth, namely Islam; idols have no true call and do not answer those who invoke them.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r6.anchor: وقيل: (له دعوة الحق) ي الدعاء إلى الحق وهو الإسلام

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r7.claim: Those who call on others besides God are the polytheists who have made idols into lords.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r7.anchor: والذين يدعون يعني يدعون المشركين من دونه أي: من دون الله فدعوا الأوثان أربابا

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r8.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says they call on idols to meet their needs.

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r9.speaker: مجاهد، والأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r9.claim: Mujahid and al-Asamm compare idol worshippers to someone calling to water and gesturing with his hand, but the water does not come.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r9.anchor: فقيل: كباسط كفيه إلى الماء يدعو الماء بلسانه ويشير إليه بيده فلا يأتيه، عن مجاهد، والأصم

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r10.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r10.claim: Abu Ali understands the image as someone trying to reach water with an outstretched hand.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r10.anchor: وقيل: يريد أن يصل إلى تناول الماء بيده على بسطها، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r11.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says the person dies before he can reach the water.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r11.anchor: وقيل: كباسط كفيه إلى الماء فمات قبل أن يصل، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r12.speaker: علي، وعطاء، وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r12.claim: Ali, Ata, and Abu Muslim picture a thirsty person at a well without a bucket, reaching for water that neither comes up nor reaches him; likewise idols neither answer nor benefit their worshippers.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r12.anchor: وقيل: كعطشان على ساقية، ولا دلو معه يمد يده إلى البئر، فلا يبلغ الماء، ولا يرتفع الماء إليه

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas compares them to a thirsty person who sees water far away but cannot reach it.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r13.anchor: وقيل: كعطشان يرى الماء من بعيد يريد أن يتناوله فلا يقدر عليه، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r14.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r14.claim: The judge's closest reading is someone gesturing toward water and hoping it will reach his mouth, though it cannot.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r14.anchor: وقيل: كمشير إليه يريد بهذا القدر أن يبلغ فاه فلا يبلغ، عن القاضي، قال: وهو الأقرب

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r15.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r15.claim: Al-Dahhak, reporting from Ibn Abbas, says an outstretched hand cannot help a thirsty person, just as idols can neither benefit nor harm their worshippers.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r15.anchor: وقيل: كما أن العطشان لا ينفعه بسط الكف إلى الماء كذلك الأوثان لا تملك لهم نفعا ولا ضرا، عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r16.speaker: أبو عبيدة، والقتبي، وأبو مسلم، وأبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r16.claim: They explain the image as a person pursuing what cannot be attained, like someone grasping water; a poem uses the same comparison for lost affection.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r16.anchor: وقيل: إنه مثل لمن يسعى فيما لا يدرك، فيقال: هو كالقابض على الماء، عن أبي عبيدة، و[القتبي]، وأبي مسلم، وأبي القاسم

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r17.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r17.claim: The poet compares former affection to someone clutching water in his hand, illustrating an unattainable thing.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r17.anchor: قال الشاعر: وأصبحت مما كان بيني وبينها ... من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r18.claim: The phrase in ضلال has been explained as being in ruin or perdition.

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r19.claim: Another explanation is that the unbelievers' invocation strays from what is correct.

JISHUMI:v5p3767/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r20.claim: A further gloss is that it misses the path to answer and benefit, and thus departs from the true invocation.
JISHUMI:v5p3767/r20.anchor: وقيل: عن طريق الإجابة والنفع، كأنه قيل: في ضلال عن دعوة الحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r1.claim: One reading attaches the call to truth, like كلمة الحق: it is exclusively true, and God answers and grants what benefits the petitioner because He alone is worthy of prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r1.anchor: أن تضاف الدعوة إلى الحق الذي هو نقيض الباطل ، كما تضاف الكلمة إليه في قولك : كلمة الحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is the call directed to the True One, God, who hears and answers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r2.anchor: والثاني : أن تضاف إلى الحق الذي هو الله عز وعلا ، على معنى : دعوة المدعو الحق الذي يسمع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r3.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says al-Haqq means God, and every invocation directed to Him is the true invocation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن : الحق هو الله ، وكل دعاء إليه دعوة الحق .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r4.claim: The phrase connects with the account of Arbad: the thunderbolt was God's unseen counterplot, and the Prophet's prayer against the two men was answered.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r4.anchor: أما على قصة أربد فظاهر ؛ لأن إصابته بالصاعقة محال من الله ومكر به من حيث لم يشعر .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r5.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r5.claim: The Prophet prayed that God strike Arbad and his companion as He wished; the prayer was answered, making it a true invocation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r5.anchor: دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عليه وعلى صاحبه بقوله : ( اللهم اخسفهما بما شئت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r6.claim: On the first interpretation, the verse threatens unbelievers with God's destruction and with His answering the Prophet if he prays against them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r6.anchor: وأما على الأول فوعيد للكفرة على مجادلتهم رسول الله بحلول محاله بهم ، وإجابة دعوة رسول الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r7.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols worshipped by unbelievers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r7.anchor: والآلهة الذين يدعوهم الكفار { من } دون الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r8.claim: Their helplessness resembles a person extending both hands to water and asking it to reach his mouth: water cannot sense or answer thirst, and neither can idols.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r8.anchor: والماء جماد لا يشعر ببسط كفيه ولا بعطشه وحاجته إليه ، ولا يقدر أن يجيب دعاءه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r9.claim: Alternatively, the image is of someone spreading his fingers into water to scoop a drink, yet gathering none and failing to satisfy his request.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r9.anchor: وقيل : شبهوا في قلة جدوى دعائهم لآلهتهم بمن أراد أن يغرف الماء بيديه ليشربه ،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r10.claim: A variant reads تدعون with direct address instead of the third-person form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r10.anchor: وقرىء : ( تدعون ) بالتاء . كباسط كفيه ، بالتنوين { إلا فى ضلال }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r11.claim: Another reported reading places nunation on باسط.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r11.anchor: وقرىء : ( تدعون ) بالتاء . كباسط كفيه ، بالتنوين { إلا فى ضلال }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r12.claim: ضلال is loss without benefit: unbelievers' calls to God receive no answer, while their idols cannot answer them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p490/r12.anchor: إلا في ضياع لا منفعة فيه ؛ لأنهم إن دعوا الله لم يجبهم ، وإن دعوا الآلهة لم تستطع إجابتهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the true call is the testimony “There is no god but God.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r1.anchor: أن دعوة الحق لا إله إلا الله , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God is the Real, so calling upon Him is the true call.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r3.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r3.claim: Some later commentators identify the true call as sincere devotion in supplication.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r3.anchor: أن الإخلاص في الدعاء هي دعوة الحق , قاله بعض المتأخرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r4.claim: A further possible sense, fitting the context, is calling upon God in danger, when no one else is invoked; the next phrase concerns idols invoked besides Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r4.anchor: دعاؤه عند الخوف لأنه لا يدعى فيه إلا إياه , كما قال تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r5.claim: The idols neither answer their supplications nor hear their calls.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r5.anchor: أي لا يجيبون لهم دعاء ولا يسمعون لهم نداء

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r6.claim: The water simile expresses despair of an answer; Arabs use reaching for water by hand as an example of striving for what cannot be attained.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r6.anchor: ضرب الله عز وجل الماء مثلا لإياسهم من إجابة دعائهم لأن العرب تضرب لمن سعى فيما لا يدركه مثلا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r7.claim: Abū al-Hudhayl’s line compares a lost bond of affection to someone grasping water by hand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r7.anchor: مثلا بالقابض الماء باليد , كما قال أبو الهذيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r8.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r8.claim: Mujāhid compares the idolater to a thirsty person calling distant water toward his mouth, motioning with his hand but unable to attain it; the water does not answer or come.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r8.anchor: وما الماء ببالغ إليه , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares the idolater to a thirsty person reaching toward a reflection of water, deceived by a false impression that cannot bring it to his mouth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r9.anchor: لكذب ظنه وفساد توهمه , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r10.claim: A third explanation is someone stretching a hand toward water to grasp it, but getting nothing in his palm.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r10.anchor: كباسط كفه إلى الماء ليقبض عليه فلا يحصل في كفيه شيء منه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r11.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says “water” means a well, its source; the example is reaching into a well without a rope, as the following poem indicates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p103/r11.anchor: المراد بالماء ها هنا البئر لأنها معدن للماء , وأن المثل كمن مد يده إلى البئر بغير رشاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104/r1.claim: An unnamed poet’s line about an inherited well that he dug and lined supports al-Farrāʾ’s reading of water as a well.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104/r1.anchor: فإن الماء ماء أبي وجدي … وبئري ذو حفرت وذو طويت

MUJAHID:v1p326#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p326#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p326#2/r1.claim: The idolater calls to water with his tongue and gestures toward it with his hands, but it never comes to him.
MUJAHID:v1p326#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ﴾ يقول يدعو الماء بلسانه ويشير إليه بيديه فلا يأتيه أبدا

MUQATIL:13:14/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:14/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:14/r1.claim: The true invocation means the declaration of sincerity and divine unity.
MUQATIL:13:14/r1.anchor: له دعوة الحق } ، يعني كلمة الإخلاص

MUQATIL:13:14/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:14/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:14/r2.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols that people worship.
MUQATIL:13:14/r2.anchor: يعني والذين يعبدون من دون الله

MUQATIL:13:14/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:14/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:14/r3.claim: Idols neither answer their worshippers nor benefit them, like water that a thirsty man at a well's edge calls toward his mouth but cannot reach, until he dies of thirst.
MUQATIL:13:14/r3.anchor: كما لا ينفع العطشان الماء يبسط يده إلى الماء

MUQATIL:13:14/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:14/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:14/r4.claim: Calling the idols means worshipping them, and the worship of disbelievers is loss and falsehood.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r1.claim: The genitive links supplication to truth, separating it from falsehood: God merits prayer because it brings benefit, unlike calls to useless idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r1.anchor: أضيفت إلى الحق الذي هو ضد الباطل للدلالة على أن الدعوة ملابسة للحق وأنها بمعزل من الباطل والمعنى أن الله سبحانه يدعى فيستجيب الدعوة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r2.claim: Connection to the preceding severe stratagem evokes Arbad's death by thunderbolt and the Prophet's answered prayer against Arbad and his companion.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r2.anchor: واتصال شديد المحال له ودعوة الحق بما قبله على قصة أربد ظاهر لأن اصابته بالصاعقة محال من الله ومكر به من حيث لم يشعر وقد دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عليه وعلى صاحبه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r3.claim: Alternatively, this warns disbelievers that God's severe stratagem will befall them and the Prophet's prayer against them will be answered.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r3.anchor: وعلى الأول وعيد للكفرة على مجادلتهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحلول محاله بهم وإجابة دعوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيهم ان دعا عليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r4.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols worshipped by unbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r4.anchor: ﴿ والذين يدعون ﴾ والآلهة الذين يدعوهم الكفار ﴿ من دونه ﴾ من دون الله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r5.claim: The idols do not answer any requests.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r6.claim: The exception is from the verbal noun implied by “they do not answer”; a verb also implies time, place, and manner, each of which can be excepted.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r6.anchor: استثناء من المصدر اي من الاستجابة التي دل عليها لا يستجيبون لأن الفعل بحروفه يدل على المصدر وبصيغته على الزمان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r7.claim: The thirsty person's hands cannot make water reach his mouth; likewise idols are insensate and cannot hear, answer, or help worshippers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r7.anchor: وكذلك ما يدعونه جماد لا يحس بدعائهم ولا يستطيع إجابتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r8.claim: The pronoun refers to the water: it will not reach the supplicant's mouth.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r9.claim: The unbelievers' calls are futile: God does not answer them, and idols cannot answer them.
