NASAFI-FULL:v2p213/r9.anchor: في ضياع لا منفعة فيه لأنهم إن دعوا الله لم يجبهم وان دعوا الأصنام لم تستطع اجابتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and others say the true invocation is the declaration that there is no god but God.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة وغيرهما: لا إله إلا الله

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God is the Real, so calling upon Him is the true invocation.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: إن الله هو الحق، فدعاؤه دعوة الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r3.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r3.claim: Some later exegetes interpret the true invocation as sincerity in supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن الإخلاص في الدعاء هو دعوة الحق قاله بعض المتأخرين

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r4.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī says it is calling on God in fear, when no one but Him is invoked, linking it to 17:67; he considers this closest to the context about idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r4.anchor: قال الماوردي: وهو أشبه بسياق الآية لأنه قال: { والذين يدعون من دونه }

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r5.claim: Those invoked besides God are idols and images.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r5.anchor: يعني الأصنام والأوثان. { لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء }

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r6.claim: The idols neither answer their prayer nor hear their cries.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r6.anchor: أي لا يستجيبون لهم دعاء، ولا يسمعون لهم نداء

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r7.claim: The water image shows how hopeless it is to expect idols to answer: Arabs liken an unattainable pursuit to someone grasping water by hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r7.anchor: ضرب الله عز وجل الماء مثلا ليأسهم من الإجابة لدعائهم لأن العرب تضرب لمن سعى فيما لا يدركه مثلا

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r8.claim: Mujāhid compares the idol worshipper to a thirsty person calling water from afar and reaching with tongue and hand without obtaining it; water does not answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r8.anchor: وما الماء ببالغ إليه قاله مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares the person to a thirsty man reaching toward his reflection in water, deceived by his mistaken perception.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r9.anchor: لكذب ظنه، وفساد توهمه قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r10.claim: A third interpretation is someone stretching a hand to seize water, but nothing solid gathers in his palm.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r10.anchor: الثالث: أنه كباسط كفه إلى الماء ليقبض عليه فلا يجمد في كفه شيء منه

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r11.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes water to mean a well, its source, and compares the futile act to reaching into a well without a rope; a poem mentions a family's well.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r11.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن المراد بالماء هاهنا البئر لأنها معدن للماء

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r12.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r12.claim: ʿAlī compares it to a thirsty person at a well's edge who cannot reach its bottom, while the water does not rise to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r12.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: هو كالعطشان على شفة البئر، فلا يبلغ قعر البئر

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r13.claim: The cited poem uses grasping water by hand to signify an unattainable object.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r13.anchor: فأصبحت فيما كان بيني وبينها من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r14.claim: The phrase means like the response to someone extending both hands toward water; a verbal noun is annexed to its doer with an understood complement omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r14.anchor: ومعنى «إلا كباسط» إلا كاستجابة باسط كفيه «إلى الماء»

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r15.claim: The purpose lām in li-yablugha is attached to the act of stretching the hands.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r15.anchor: واللام في قوله: «ليبلغ فاه» متعلقة بالبسط

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r16.claim: The pronoun may refer to water, which will not reach the mouth, or to the mouth, which cannot reach the water.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r16.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «هو» كناية عن الفم أي ما الفم ببالغ الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r17.claim: The disbelievers' worship of idols is misguidance because it is shirk.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r17.anchor: أي ليست عبادة الكافرين الأصنام إلا في ضلال، لأنها شرك

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r18.claim: Alternatively, their invocation goes astray from them and yields no path to its object, as in 7:37.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14/r18.anchor: وقيل: إلا في ضلال أي يضل عنهم ذلك الدعاء، فلا يجدون منه سبيلا

QURTUBI-FULL:13:14#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the disbelievers' voices are veiled from God, so He does not hear their invocation.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:14#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أي أصوات الكافرين محجوبة عن الله فلا يسمع دعاءهم

BURSEVI:v4p233/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r1.claim: The phrase can mean the idols whom disbelievers invoke, with a resumptive pronoun omitted, or the disbelievers who invoke idols, with the object omitted.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r1.anchor: والأصنام الذين يدعونهم الكفار متجاوزين الله في الدعاء إلى الأصنام فحذف الراجع ، أو والكفار الذين يدعون الأصنام من دونه تعالى فحذف المفعول

BURSEVI:v4p233/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r2.claim: The idols are given a rational plural pronoun because polytheists treat them like rational beings.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r2.anchor: وضمير العقلاء لمعاملتهم إياها معاملة العقلاء

BURSEVI:v4p233/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r3.claim: The idols do not answer the disbelievers' wishes with anything.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r3.anchor: لهم أي : الكفار بشيء من مراداتهم

BURSEVI:v4p233/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r4.claim: This is an exception from the broadest class of verbal nouns, meaning a response only like that of someone extending his hands toward water.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r4.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من أعم عام المصدر أي إلا استجابة مثل استجابة ماد يديه

BURSEVI:v4p233/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p233/r5.claim: Al-Kashifi pictures a thirsty traveler with no bucket or rope spreading both hands and pleading for water.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (مكر همون اجابت كسى كه بكشاده هرد وكف خودار بسوى آب

BURSEVI:v4p233/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r6.claim: The thirsty person calls to the water with his tongue and gestures, the لام attaches to باسط, and water is the subject of يبلغ.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r6.anchor: أي : يدعو الماء بلسانه ويشير إليه بيده ليصل إلى فمه فاللام متعلق بباسط ففاعل يبلغ هو الماء

BURSEVI:v4p233/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r7.claim: The water cannot reach the mouth because it is inert, unaware of the hands or thirst, and unable to benefit the caller.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r7.anchor: لأنه جماد لا يشعر ببسط كفيه ولا بعطشه وحاجته إليه ولا يقدر على نفعهم

BURSEVI:v4p233/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r8.claim: This is a compound parable: the idols' failure to respond or help resembles water before a thirsty person whose gestures cannot make it reach him; the parallel has several parts.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r8.anchor: والتشبيه من المركب التمثيلي شبه حال الأصنام مع من دعاءهم من المشركين وهو عدم استجابتهم دعاء المشركين وعدم فوز المشركين من دعائهم الأصنام شيئا من الاستجابة والنفع بحال الماء

BURSEVI:v4p233/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r9.claim: Calling on idols is loss, waste, and falsehood because they cannot answer.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r9.anchor: وما دعاء الكافرين يعني لأصنامهم إلا في ضلال في ضياع وخسار وباطل ، لأن الآلهة لا تقدر على إجابتهم

BURSEVI:v4p233/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r10.claim: Kalam and legal works allow God to answer a disbeliever's prayer; He answered Iblis and others, and Pharaoh privately prayed during low Nile water and was answered.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r10.anchor: وأما دعاؤهم له تعالى فالمذهب جواز استجابته كما في كتب الكلام والفتاوى ، وقد أجاب الله دعاء إبليس وغيره

BURSEVI:v4p233/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r11.claim: Since God does not waste even a disbeliever's prayer, a believer has still greater reason to hope for a response.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r11.anchor: فإذا كان الله لا يضيع دعاء الكافرين فما ظنك بالمؤمن

BURSEVI:v4p233/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233/r12.claim: Although water naturally sinks, God can move it upward contrary to its nature as a miracle; some saints reaching the ultimate cause may dispense with ordinary means.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r12.anchor: والماء وإن كان من طبعه التسفل ولكن الله تعالى إذا أراد يحركه من المركز إلى جانب المحيط على خلاف طبعه بطريق خرق العادة

BURSEVI:v4p233/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233/r13.speaker: أبو عبد الله بن خفيف
BURSEVI:v4p233/r13.claim: The author begins a story in which the Sufi shaykh Ibn Khafif says he entered Baghdad intending to make the pilgrimage, carrying Sufi resolve and ascetic discipline.
BURSEVI:v4p233/r13.anchor: حكي عن الشيخ أبي عبد الله بن حفيف رضي الله عنه قال : دخلت بغداد قاصدا الحج وفي رأسي نخوة الصوفية

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r1.claim: The phrase means that God possesses the true invocation or call.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r1.anchor: اعلم أن قوله : { له دعوة الحق } أي لله دعوة الحق

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r2.claim: Ikrima transmits from Ibn Abbas that ‘the invocation of truth’ is the declaration ‘There is no deity but God.’
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r2.anchor: ما روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : { دعوة الحق } قول لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says God is the Real, so calling upon Him is true, alluding to directing supplication solely to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r3.anchor: قول الحسن : إن الله هو الحق ، فدعاؤه هو الحق ، كأنه يومىء إلى أن الانقطاع إليه في الدعاء هو الحق

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that God’s worship is true and genuine.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r4.anchor: وثالثها : أن عبادته هي الحق والصدق

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r5.claim: Al-Razi argues that contingent beings may cease to exist, but the Necessary Existent cannot; God is therefore the truest existent, and affirming, remembering, and praising Him are the truest belief and invocation.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r5.anchor: وإذا كان واجب الوجود لذاته موجودا لا يقبل العدم كان أحق الموجودات بأن يكون حقا هو هو

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r6.claim: One al-Kashshaf construction adds دعوة to الحق as a quality, like كلمة الحق: the invocation is wholly true and free of signs of falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r6.anchor: أن تضاف الدعوة إلى الحق الذي هو نقيض الباطل كما تضاف إليه الكلمة في قوله : { كلمة * الحق }

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r7.claim: A second construction makes الحق God: it is the invocation of the Real who hears and answers; al-Hasan likewise says every call to God is the true invocation.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r7.anchor: أن تضاف إلى الحق الذي هو الله سبحانه على معنى دعوة المدعو الحق الذي يسمع فيجيب

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r8.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols called upon by unbelievers; like water, they cannot sense a plea or thirst, answer, or benefit their worshippers.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r8.anchor: يعني الآلهة الذين يدعونهم الكفار من دون الله : { لا يستجيبون لهم بشىء }

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r9.claim: The image compares their futile calls to extending one’s palms toward insensible water, which cannot reach the mouth or satisfy thirst.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r9.anchor: والماء جماد لا يشعر ببسط كفيه ولا بعطشه وحاجته إليه ، ولا يقدر أن يجيب دعاءه ويبلغ فاه

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r10.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r10.claim: Another explanation compares the prayer to trying to scoop water with spread fingers: the hands cannot reach it, so the person never drinks.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r10.anchor: وقيل شبهوا في قلة فائد دعائهم لآلهتهم ، بمن أراد أن يغرف الماء بيديه ليشربه

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r11.claim: A variant reads تدعون with second-person tāʾ; كباسط كفيه is also read with tanwīn.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r11.anchor: وقرىء { تدعون } بالتاء { كباسط كفيه } بالتنوين

RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r12.claim: Unbelievers’ prayers are wasted: God does not answer them, while the idols lack the ability to respond.
RAZI-FULL:v19p23#3/r12.anchor: أي إلا في ضياع لا منفعة فيه ، لأنهم إن دعوا الله لم يجبهم وإن دعوا الآلهة لم تستطع إجابتهم
